biosec.name: AI and Biosecurity

units.title: The map: assistance, execution and oversight
units.desc: Locate the biological bottleneck, then identify the checkpoint a policy can actually reach.

lessons.title: From AI advice to physical effects

items.p: A staffer is mapping AI-related biological risk. Which set of checkpoints best organizes the assessment?
o: AI assistance, physical execution, and the oversight at each checkpoint
Training compute, benchmark rank, and release date
Research funding, company ownership, and publication count
Model size, scientific citations, and subscription price
ow: These describe a model without identifying where it changes biological work.
These can inform oversight but miss capability and physical execution.
These are poor substitutes for checking assistance, execution and controls.
keys: AI assistance, physical execution, and the oversight at each checkpoint
items.x: Start with the assistance AI provides, then ask what physical work remains and which controls apply. The course follows that map through evidence, lab safeguards, synthesis screening and public rules.

items.p: A novice can explain a laboratory procedure after consulting AI. Why does that leave an important biological-risk question unanswered?
o: Explaining a procedure does not prove execution
Correctly recalling the steps establishes practical skill
Success on a simulated exercise establishes success in a real laboratory
A successful demonstration establishes this user can repeat it
ow: Knowing the steps and carrying them out are distinct kinds of performance.
Simulation can leave out physical skills and environmental constraints.
A demonstration does not establish repeatable performance by the learner.
keys: Explaining a procedure does not prove execution
items.x: The Los Alamos pilot distinguishes knowledge assistance from skill assistance. Practical execution can remain a barrier even when a user can describe the work.

items.p: Match each AI application to the extra checkpoint it makes relevant.
pairs: Check whether advice is accurate and useful to the user
Check the proposed design and its physical production
Check authorization for experiments and physical operations
items.x: Research assistance, design and automation can interact. CRS describes both AI-generated sequences and AI use in autonomous laboratories; neither makes physical testing unnecessary.

items.p: Why can synthetic DNA manufacturing remain a useful biosecurity checkpoint when protein designs come from many different AI tools?
items.answer: A computational design must be physically produced to have biological effects, so manufacturing offers a checkpoint shared by different design tools.
keys: physical production is needed
a shared manufacturing checkpoint

o: Different design tools converge on physical production
Providers can infer buyers' intentions
Sequence screening establishes that research is safe
A design model needs a synthesis company's prior approval
ow: Customer checks provide evidence about legitimacy, rather than certainty about intent.
Screening can miss hazards and does not certify the whole research project.
The checkpoint is manufacturing; it is not a general approval power over software.

items.x: Responsible AI x Biodesign signatories identify DNA manufacturing as a useful checkpoint. Its value depends on coverage and screening quality, which later lessons examine.

units.title: What the evidence establishes
units.desc: Start with physical trials, then compare what benchmarks, table top exercises and incident reports can show.

items.p: A 2025 randomized trial gave 153 novices AI plus internet access or internet access alone for laboratory tasks. What happened to completion of the whole workflow?
o: There was no statistically significant difference in whole-workflow completion
AI access significantly increased completion
Internet-only users did significantly better
Completion was too common to compare groups
ow: The primary endpoint did not show a statistically significant increase.
The internet arm was numerically higher, without a significant difference.
Completion was uncommon in both arms, rather than too common.
keys: There was no statistically significant difference in whole-workflow completion
items.x: The trial reported 5.2% completion with AI and 6.6% with internet alone. Some measures suggested modest benefits, so this result should narrow claims about the tested setting rather than erase all concern.

items.p: A staffer sees the trial's nonsignificant result described as proof of zero AI uplift. Which correction is warranted?
o: The study did not establish that the effect was zero
Randomization eliminates uncertainty
A nonsignificant result reveals a large hidden benefit
Lower AI completion proves that AI made participants worse
ow: Randomization helps identify effects but does not eliminate statistical uncertainty.
The result leaves uncertainty; it does not establish a large benefit.
A numerical difference without statistical support does not establish harm.
keys: The study did not establish that the effect was zero
items.x: A nonsignificant result can be compatible with several effect sizes. The paper also reports exploratory analyses, which deserve less weight than its preregistered primary endpoint.

items.p: Name two features of the 2025 novice trial that limit applying its result to all AI-related biological risks.
items.answer: It tested novices rather than expert users, and it tested mid-2025 models on selected laboratory tasks rather than every model or pathway.
keys: novice population
mid-2025 models and selected tasks

o: It covered one user population and a bounded set of tasks
It had no comparison group or physical laboratory
It tested experts without access to the internet
It measured publication quality rather than completion rates
ow: The study had an internet-only comparison group and physical laboratory tasks.
The participants were novices, and the comparison group had internet access.
Laboratory workflow completion was the primary endpoint.

items.x: Retrieve the map: changing the user, the AI system or the physical task can change the bottleneck. METR also stresses that trials measure how participants use a model alongside its capabilities.

items.p: A small Los Alamos laboratory pilot suggested AI-assisted participants could do better. How should it affect the reading of the larger novice trial?
o: Treat it as suggestive evidence about AI assistance in a different setting
Replace the larger trial with this positive finding
Average the headlines before comparing the tasks
Discard it because laboratory studies cannot test uplift
ow: A positive result does not outweigh study size and design by itself.
Different tasks and endpoints need comparison before quantitative pooling.
Physical trials directly inform questions that written tests cannot settle.
keys: Treat it as suggestive evidence about AI assistance in a different setting
items.x: The Los Alamos paper presents a pilot and lessons for future studies. Different samples and tasks can produce different results without a contradiction.

items.p: Match each biosecurity evidence source to the most direct question it answers.
pairs: How well does the model answer these technical questions?
How much does AI access change performance on these tasks?
What proposals can these teams produce with the model?
What activity did this provider observe and investigate?
items.x: These are complementary views. A tabletop can reveal scientific errors, while a controlled trial can estimate an access effect; neither alone establishes the frequency of harmful outcomes.

items.p: A model beats specialists on a virology question benchmark. Which claim follows most directly?
o: It performs strongly on that benchmark
It reliably replaces specialists in a physical laboratory
It increases human workflow completion by the same margin
Its deployed safeguards failed against real malicious users
ow: Question-answering performance does not establish physical execution.
A benchmark margin does not translate directly into a human uplift effect.
Capability questions do not measure deployed safeguards or users' intent.
keys: It performs strongly on that benchmark
items.x: The 2025 VCT paper reported that OpenAI o3 outscored its expert comparison group. That result motivates closer assessment; it does not demonstrate end-to-end laboratory competence.

items.p: OpenAI counts identified refusals as successes in one reported biological capability score. What should a staffer infer from that adjusted score?
o: An upper-bound capability estimate under that scoring rule
It measures the rate of successful harmful deployment
It shows accurate answers were supplied to those requests
It estimates how often ordinary users can bypass safeguards
ow: The adjusted score concerns potential capability, not harmful outcomes.
A refusal did not supply an answer; the scoring rule assigns credit anyway.
A refusal-adjusted score is not a jailbreak success rate.
keys: upper-bound capability estimate under the refusal scoring rule
items.x: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra card calls the adjustment an upper bound. Changes in refusal behavior can move this score even when underlying scientific capability changes less.

items.p: In a biology tabletop, the best team lacks the specialty being tested, while specialist teams do better on average. Why is the winning team insufficient evidence that AI replaces that specialty?
items.answer: One winning team does not establish reliable replacement across teams. Stronger specialist performance on average leaves a skill gap despite the standout result.
keys: single standout result does not establish reliable substitution across teams
specialists did better on average

o: A standout team does not establish reliable replacement
Ignoring the winning proposal is warranted whenever generalists beat specialists
The average proves AI gave no useful help
A tabletop automatically measures physical laboratory success
ow: The standout result is evidence, and should be considered alongside the rest.
All teams had AI, so the average gap does not identify AI's causal benefit.
A proposal exercise does not demonstrate physical execution.

items.x: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 tabletop gave every team a model. The company reports both a generalist winner and stronger pooled specialist results, alongside errors. Without a no-AI arm, the exercise cannot isolate causal uplift.

units.title: How labs gate biological assistance
units.desc: Compare threat scenarios and assess uncertainty, layered defenses and trusted access.

items.p: OpenAI treats GPT-6 Astra as High biological capability while judging it below Critical. What does that distinction describe?
o: They describe different biological threat scenarios within OpenAI's own framework
They describe two levels of government approval
They predict which designs synthesis providers accept
They are identical international categories used by all labs
ow: These are OpenAI capability categories, rather than government permits.
Synthesis screening is a separate physical checkpoint.
Lab definitions differ, so the labels cannot be equated automatically.
keys: They describe different biological threat scenarios within OpenAI's own framework
items.x: In Astra's October 2026 card, High concerns meaningful help to novices with known severe threats. Critical concerns expert uplift toward a dangerous novel threat or a full engineering cycle without human intervention.

items.p: Match each framework or measurement to what it represents.
pairs: Company categories concerning non-novel / novel weapons
Company thresholds tied to specified threat scenarios
A scientific question-answering benchmark, rather than a release rule
items.x: As of October 2026, Anthropic and OpenAI use different definitions and supporting evidence. Compare the underlying scenario and required safeguards before comparing category names.

items.p: A lab cannot rule out a biological capability threshold but says deployment controls make release manageable. Which evidence most directly tests that claim?
o: Stress tests of the deployed safeguards on relevant access routes
A higher score on an unguarded scientific question benchmark
Customer identity checks for one vetted institutional access tier
A comparable model receiving a similar category label at a competing lab
ow: An unguarded benchmark informs capability, rather than the protection provided by deployed safeguards.
Vetting one route leaves other access routes and continuing safeguards untested.
Other labs can use different definitions, and a label does not establish this deployment's controls.
keys: test deployed safeguards against the relevant threat scenarios and access routes
items.x: OpenAI precautionarily treats Astra as High while noting that wet-lab studies could change its assessment. Capability classification and the adequacy of deployment controls are distinct judgments.

items.p: Why does OpenAI argue that blocking repeated biological assistance can matter even if one unsafe answer slips through?
o: A harmful effort may need sustained tailored assistance
One refusal establishes durable protection
Every biological question carries equal risk
Safeguard failures are statistically independent across steps
ow: A refusal in one interaction does not establish durable protection.
Different questions can have very different relevance and consequences.
Shared failure modes can correlate failures across steps and safeguards.
keys: A harmful effort may need sustained tailored assistance
items.x: Astra's card hypothesizes that repeated troubleshooting creates opportunities for refusals, blocks and enforcement. This is a threat-model argument, not proof that layered controls achieve a particular failure rate.

items.p: A provider offers less restricted biological assistance to vetted institutions. Name two checks needed to assess that access policy.
items.answer: Examples: how institutions and individual users are verified; what uses are authorized; what monitoring continues after admission; how access can be suspended; whether third-party access is controlled.

o: Vetting standards and controls after admission
Subscription terms and published model benchmark scores
Research publications and the institution's citation count
Model launch date and provider market share
ow: These concern service terms and capability, rather than identity, authorization and continuing access controls.
Publications can inform a review but do not establish authorized use or continuing safeguards.
Age and market share do not establish how trusted access is governed.
choice.p: Which pair of checks helps assess trusted access to sensitive biological assistance?

items.x: OpenAI describes trusted-access programs alongside monitoring and enforcement. These are questions for assessing the program, rather than claims that institutional affiliation eliminates misuse risk.

items.p: Anthropic reported a reseller directing refused biological requests to other providers. Which policy lesson does that support?
o: Assess safeguards across providers and intermediaries
Classify reseller users as malicious
Infer that refused requests caused a harmful outbreak
Treat one provider's refusal rate as protection across the ecosystem
ow: Anthropic explicitly declined to assert harmful intent for the scientists.
The report describes concerning use and access evasion, not a demonstrated outbreak.
Users can interact with intermediaries and providers with different controls.
keys: Assess safeguards across providers and intermediaries
items.x: The September 2026 report is Anthropic's account of observed activity. It supports scrutiny of cross-provider coverage; it does not establish harmful intent or the overall rate of biological misuse.

units.title: Controls beyond the model
units.desc: Connect synthesis screening and funding conditions with domestic regulation, treaties and export coordination.

items.p: A 2025 screening study found AI-redesigned sequences that existing tools detected unreliably. What policy implication follows from the team's subsequent patches?
o: Screening performance needs repeated testing and updates as design tools change
Every screening tool is ineffective
A patched detector certifies the whole project
Sequence screening should replace customer verification
ow: The team improved detection, which contradicts a blanket claim of ineffectiveness.
Detection is one checkpoint and does not certify the whole project.
Sequence and customer screening address different questions.
keys: Screening performance needs repeated testing and updates as design tools change
items.x: The Paraphrase Project reports working with four synthesis companies to improve detection. Keep the claim bounded: a demonstrated screening weakness and mitigation do not measure real-world weapon development.

items.p: HHS guidance expanded screening beyond sequences unique to regulated agents. What is the scope principle?
o: Screen for contributions to pathogenicity or toxicity
Use regulated-agent list membership as the sole criterion for concern
Replace sequence review with institution names
Treat all nucleic acid sequences as equally hazardous
ow: The expanded definition includes concern from unregulated agents.
Institutional checks complement rather than replace sequence screening.
The guidance distinguishes sequences of concern from other sequences.
keys: Screen for contributions to pathogenicity or toxicity
items.x: The 2023 guidance broadens its definition to regulated and unregulated sources as practical. This is a screening recommendation, rather than proof that every potentially concerning sequence can already be identified.

items.p: Match each synthesis screening component to its purpose.
pairs: Resolve concerns before fulfilling an order
items.x: These checks can run in parallel, so they do not form one universal timeline. IGSC describes sequence screening and customer vetting; HHS also recommends verification and records for relevant transfers.

items.p: A federally funded US lab orders synthetic DNA from an overseas supplier. Does foreign location alone remove the 2024 federal screening condition?
items.answer: No. The condition follows the funded purchaser: it must procure from a compliant supplier, including when that supplier is overseas.
keys: funding condition follows purchaser
foreign supplier must meet procurement condition

o: No, the condition follows the funded purchaser
Yes, federal funding conditions stop at national borders
Yes, foreign suppliers are governed by voluntary membership alone
No, the framework directly licenses every supplier worldwide
ow: The condition restricts procurement by the funded customer.
The funding condition requires a compliant supplier; membership alone is not the rule.
Procurement leverage differs from directly licensing all suppliers.

items.x: The 2024 framework ties compliance to US governmental life sciences funding. A buyer outside that funding relationship may escape this particular lever, while other laws or contract terms can still apply.

items.p: As of October 2026, what distinguishes the nucleic acid screening framework from the newer high-risk research policy?
o: One governs procurement; the other governs research funding
They are the same renamed policy
One tests AI; the other checks identity
Both directly prohibit every privately funded biological project
ow: ASPR describes separate policies with different subjects.
Screening concerns synthesis procurement; research oversight concerns risky research.
Their funding mechanisms do not establish a universal ban on private research.
keys: One governs procurement; the other governs research funding
items.x: ASPR says the July 2026 high-risk research policy replaced the 2024 research oversight policy. Its screening page separately says the 2024 synthesis framework awaits revision. Replacing one policy does not establish that the other was replaced.

items.p: A facility will possess a listed select agent. Which federal program specifically regulates possession, use and transfer?
o: The Federal Select Agent Program
The International Gene Synthesis Consortium
The Australia Group export-control secretariat
The Biological Weapons Convention Implementation Support Unit
ow: IGSC is an industry screening consortium, rather than a federal regulator.
The Australia Group coordinates national export controls.
The treaty support unit does not register US facilities.
keys: The Federal Select Agent Program
items.x: CDC and USDA jointly administer the program and inspect covered entities. This is a specific regulatory regime; additional criminal, export and funding rules can also matter.

items.p: A staffer says an unlisted agent is beyond every federal biosecurity restriction. What is the flaw?
o: Research-funding restrictions can apply beyond select-agent list coverage
The synthesis funding condition and select-agent registration cover the same actors
A legitimate customer identity establishes that the proposed research is allowed
Voluntary synthesis membership supplies the missing federal regulatory authority
ow: Procurement conditions and facility registration apply through different legal mechanisms.
Customer legitimacy does not settle the legal status of the research activity.
Industry membership does not supply federal regulatory authority.
keys: agent-list coverage does not exhaust applicable research-funding restrictions
items.x: A select-agent coverage question differs from a research-funding question. The July 2026 policy addresses categories of risky research, so checking a list alone cannot settle all applicable oversight.

items.p: Why does the Biological Weapons Convention's ban on biological weapons leave a separate verification problem?
items.answer: A legal prohibition does not supply routine inspections or establish whether a state is complying; the BWC has consultation and complaint mechanisms without a standing inspectorate.
keys: legal ban does not establish compliance
no standing BWC inspectorate

o: Prohibition and evidence of compliance are separate
The ban applies to listed agents alone
Nuclear inspectors enforce biological compliance
The ban waits for acceptance of a challenge inspection
ow: Article I uses a general purpose criterion rather than a fixed agent list.
The BWC does not delegate inspections to the nuclear inspectorate.
Treaty obligations do not await agreement to a challenge inspection.

items.x: Article V provides consultation and cooperation; Article VI allows complaints to the Security Council. These mechanisms differ from a routine inspection system.

items.p: Why can a facility's peaceful research output be insufficient to resolve a biological-weapons compliance concern?
o: Legitimate and prohibited work can share infrastructure
The BWC prohibits dual-use facilities
Publication creates a treaty exemption
A biological facility proves the existence of a weapons program
ow: Dual-use infrastructure is not itself prohibited by the BWC.
Publishing does not exempt prohibited work from treaty obligations.
A facility can serve entirely peaceful purposes.
keys: Legitimate and prohibited work can share infrastructure
items.x: UNIDIR's verification primer emphasizes dual-use activities and the difficulty of inferring purpose. It argues for agreed evidence collection and procedures while protecting legitimate security and commercial interests.

items.p: A country implements an Australia Group control-list change. Where does the enforceable export requirement come from?
o: Its own national export-control measures, implementing the coordinated lists
A directly enforceable Australia Group treaty
An automatic order from the BWC secretariat
The synthesis industry's customer-screening protocol
ow: The Australia Group is an informal arrangement, rather than a treaty.
The BWC support machinery does not issue national export licenses.
Industry screening and national export regulation are separate mechanisms.
keys: Its own national export-control measures, implementing the coordinated lists
items.x: The Australia Group coordinates common lists and national measures. Its guidance aims to reduce chemical and biological weapons proliferation while allowing legitimate trade.

units.title: Apply the whole map
units.desc: Practice combining evidence limits, safeguards, physical checkpoints and public rules.

lessons.title: Questions for a hearing or bill review

items.p: A model scores highly on written biology tests and refuses reliably in a limited test, but has no physical trial. Which added evidence most directly addresses whether AI helps users execute real work?
o: Controlled physical-task comparisons with and without AI access
Item-level breakdowns of the existing written benchmark score
More repeated trials of the same refusal prompts used previously
An inventory of synthesis providers named in the evaluation documents
ow: A breakdown refines knowledge evidence while leaving physical execution untested.
More of the same refusal test does not measure users' physical task performance.
A provider inventory does not identify the effect of AI access on task execution.
keys: controlled comparisons test AI access effects on physical task completion
items.x: Retrieve the course map: written capability, deployed safeguards and physical execution are different evidence targets. A controlled laboratory trial addresses the added execution question in a defined setting; it still needs external-validity limits.

items.p: A bill covers US synthesis sellers but says nothing about devices used within laboratories. Name two design questions about that device gap.
items.answer: Examples: whether devices and manufacturers are covered; who installs and maintains screening; how updates and performance are checked; what records establish compliance on devices.

o: Device coverage and maintenance of device screening
Hosted AI benchmark scores and model release dates
Seller registration and the seller's online checkout process
Institutional publication counts and research citation rankings
ow: These concern model capability and timing, rather than regulation of laboratory devices.
Those checks may matter for sellers but leave devices used within laboratories unresolved.
Publication metrics do not establish device coverage or screening compliance.
choice.p: Which pair most directly addresses the bill's gap for devices used within laboratories?

items.x: HHS guidance includes benchtop manufacturers, and NIST studies emerging screening gaps. This applies those mechanisms to a hypothetical bill without assuming its final legal reach.
keys: credit any two specific questions addressing device coverage, screening implementation, maintenance, validation or records

items.p: Scientists want to release a protein-design model under the Responsible AI x Biodesign commitments. What do those commitments call for?
o: Assess meaningful risks and address them before release
Publish when accuracy clears a benchmark
Obtain the consortium's statutory research license
Withhold every design tool regardless of the risk assessment
ow: Benchmark accuracy does not replace assessing release risks.
The voluntary commitments do not create a licensing authority.
The commitments value openness alongside proportionate risk management.
keys: Assess meaningful risks and address them before release
items.x: Signatories favor open science and commit to evaluating meaningful risks before release, limiting access when unresolved risks warrant it. These are community commitments, whose effectiveness depends on implementation.

items.p: An adviser argues that good AI safeguards remove the need for synthesis screening and research oversight. Which response uses the course's map?
o: Each control addresses a different checkpoint from AI assistance to physical effects
Synthesis screening directly measures whether AI advice improves users' skills
Funding review replaces customer checks because both assess institutional legitimacy
Private lab capability categories determine national select-agent registration
ow: Synthesis screening examines orders and customers; user uplift requires different evidence.
Research-funding oversight and synthesis customer checks address different activities and requirements.
Private capability labels do not determine the legal coverage of the select-agent regime.
keys: Each control addresses a different checkpoint along the path from AI to effects
items.x: Model safeguards concern assistance, synthesis screening concerns production, and research policies concern covered work and funding. Assess coverage and failure modes at each point, including legitimate research costs.

biosec.description: How AI can affect biological risks, what evaluations establish, and how safeguards can reduce misuse.
caveat: Reviewed October 23, 2026. Lab capability and safeguard claims are attributed self-reports. Studies cover specific models, users and tasks. Public rules are simplified and may change. Policy-level treatment only; no biological methods or protocols. AI reviewed; no human review.
Drafted and independently reviewed by AI. No person has reviewed it.

chips.name: Chips and the Compute Supply Chain

units.title: The map: from design to deployed compute
units.desc: Follow design, fabrication, memory, packaging and deployment. Different rules and constraints attach to different stages.

items.p: Nvidia describes its manufacturing strategy as fabless. What does that mean?
keys: It relies on outside manufacturers to produce its chips
items.x: Nvidia's fiscal 2026 filing describes contracted wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and packaging. A US chip designer can therefore depend on production stages abroad.
items.answer: It relies on outside manufacturers to produce its chips

o: It relies on outside manufacturers to produce its chips
It sells designs for customers to fabricate themselves
It manufactures the logic but outsources its memory
It operates its own fabs and rents out spare capacity
ow: Its customers buy products; they do not normally arrange fabrication.
Nvidia also contracts out wafer fabrication.
Fabless describes relying on external fabrication rather than owning fabs.

items.p: Match each production stage to the function it supplies.
pairs: Specify the processor architecture and circuit layout
Make the chips that hold and supply working data
Connect dies and memory into a usable component
items.x: This map separates what a designer specifies from what factories and packaging facilities can deliver. A shortage at one required stage can limit finished products.

items.p: A buyer switches from Nvidia GPUs to a different designer's custom AI chips. Why might its manufacturing concentration remain?
o: Different designers can share the same foundry
Custom chips avoid fabrication and run as software
The chip designer determines the fabrication country
A different brand requires independent memory suppliers
ow: Custom chips still require physical semiconductor fabrication.
Designers contract manufacturing; their headquarters do not locate every stage.
A brand change need not change suppliers of memory or packaging.
keys: Different designers can share the same foundry
items.x: Epoch identifies TSMC as the leading common foundry for major AI chip designers. Supplier diversification should be checked stage by stage.

items.p: Why does a fabrication plant alone not establish a complete domestic AI-chip supply chain?
keys: Memory, tools and packaging may still come from elsewhere
items.x: The supply-chain map includes specialized inputs and downstream packaging. Domestic wafer production can reduce one dependency while leaving others.
items.answer: Memory, tools and packaging may still come from elsewhere

o: Memory, tools and packaging may still come from elsewhere
Fabrication plants cannot manufacture processor circuits
A chip's legal origin always follows its designer's headquarters
Moving fabrication also moves every upstream supplier automatically
ow: Fabrication is precisely the circuit-manufacturing stage.
Legal origin is a separate and more specific question than designer headquarters.
Upstream suppliers and later production stages need separate investment.

items.p: ASML is based in the Netherlands. Why does its EUV business matter for US chip-control policy?
keys: A key production tool depends on an allied supplier
items.x: ASML supplies EUV systems used for intricate layers. This illustrates why controls on production capacity depend on the supplier network and allied measures.
items.answer: A key production tool depends on an allied supplier

o: A key production tool depends on an allied supplier
Dutch ownership makes its systems immune from US-related rules
US chip designers can replace EUV with their design software
A license for one machine authorizes all later chip exports
ow: Jurisdiction depends on applicable rules, rather than ownership alone.
Design software specifies circuits; it does not physically print them.
Equipment and resulting chip transactions can face separate controls.

items.p: A memo says Nvidia's market share fell. Which detail is essential before interpreting the claim?
o: The denominator and measurement period
Whether its own chip shipments increased
Whether company revenue grew as fast as last year
Whether its latest processor has higher peak performance
ow: A company's shipments can grow while its share falls; the market definition and period still matter.
Revenue growth does not establish the relevant denominator or a comparable market-share measure.
Product performance can influence demand, but does not define which market-share statistic is being reported.
keys: The denominator and measurement period
items.x: GPU sales, accelerator revenue and installed computing capacity are different measures. Custom chips used internally may enter a compute measure while not appearing as merchant GPU sales.

items.p: A server project has enough logic dies but cannot obtain required memory packages. What does that reveal?
o: Finished-system output can be limited downstream of fabrication
The foundry must have misreported how many wafers it processed
The chip designer can replace the missing memory with more logic dies
A government license supplies the missing physical components
ow: A genuine memory shortage is compatible with adequate wafer output.
Logic and memory serve different functions and are not interchangeable inputs.
Authorization permits a transaction; it does not manufacture components.
keys: Finished-system output can be limited downstream of fabrication
items.x: Retrieve the map: fabrication, memory and packaging must align. Policy should distinguish legal permission from physical production capacity.

items.p: Why can controls on chipmaking equipment have effects that build over time?
keys: Existing installed tools can continue producing
items.x: Equipment controls can constrain expansion, upgrades or support without instantly erasing installed capacity. Spare parts, servicing and replacement availability also matter.
items.answer: Existing installed tools can continue producing

o: Existing installed tools can continue producing
Every affected factory must close immediately
Equipment restrictions automatically recall prior shipments
All later chips remain uncontrolled once tools are installed
ow: Installed capacity can survive a restriction on new equipment.
Export rules do not automatically remove previously delivered tools.
Output may face separate jurisdiction, end-user and destination rules.

units.title: Lithography, memory and packaging
units.desc: Understand why a process advance, available memory and packaged-system output are different achievements.

items.p: Leading-edge fabs use EUV and DUV lithography. How can both remain useful?
o: Different chip layers need different patterning methods
EUV makes memory while DUV makes all processor logic
DUV is used solely to inspect circuits after fabrication
EUV removes the need for every other manufacturing tool
ow: Both technologies concern patterning, rather than an exclusive logic-memory split.
DUV is a lithography technology, rather than solely an inspection method.
Lithography remains one part of a longer fabrication process.
keys: Different chip layers need different patterning methods
items.x: ASML describes EUV as a way to print the most intricate layers. Less demanding layers can still use DUV, so controlling EUV does not settle all equipment access.

items.p: SMIC has made advanced chips without EUV. What should a staffer ask before concluding that EUV restrictions have no effect?
o: What costs, yields and volumes the alternative process achieves
Whether a shipping chip counts as evidence of technical progress
Whether every process bearing a similar node name is identical
Whether a phone chip proves a full AI-server supply chain exists
ow: A shipping chip is evidence of progress, which still leaves cost and scale questions.
Similar node labels do not establish identical process performance.
A phone chip does not demonstrate all the inputs of an AI-server system.
keys: What costs, yields and volumes the alternative process achieves
items.x: TechInsights reports that SMIC's N+3 process remains less scaled than leading commercial 5nm processes. A technical milestone and economical mass production are distinct claims.

items.p: Why can extra patterning steps make a DUV-based advanced process harder to scale?
keys: More steps add processing and opportunities for defects
items.x: A workaround can be technically feasible while less efficient. Avoid inferring a numerical yield penalty without process-specific evidence.
items.answer: More steps add processing and opportunities for defects

o: More steps add processing and opportunities for defects
Multiple exposures automatically make every die unusable
Extra steps remove dependence on precision equipment
Using DUV instead of EUV changes the designer's country
ow: Additional complexity can reduce efficiency without implying zero usable output.
Repeated precision processing still depends on equipment and process control.
Manufacturing methods do not change a designer's location.

items.p: A report calls two manufacturers' processes 5nm-class. Why is that insufficient to establish parity?
keys: Node labels do not fully specify density or performance
items.x: TechInsights compares measured structures rather than relying on a label. Policy assessments should also distinguish process capability from volume and product performance.
items.answer: Node labels do not fully specify density or performance

o: Node labels do not fully specify density or performance
Identical labels require identical transistor layouts
Node labels measure the physical width of every transistor
Once a node is reached, its production yield is fixed
ow: Commercial node labels do not mandate identical layouts.
A node name is not a literal universal dimension.
Yield depends on the design and manufacturing process and can change.

items.p: Why is HBM useful in many high-end AI accelerators?
o: It supplies data at high bandwidth near the processor
It performs the accelerator's arithmetic instead of the logic die
It replaces the need to package and connect multiple components
It makes performance independent of the model's memory needs
ow: HBM is memory; the processor still performs computations.
HBM must be integrated into a system with suitable connections.
Workload characteristics still affect how valuable bandwidth is.
keys: It supplies data at high bandwidth near the processor
items.x: HBM combines stacked memory with wide connections. Its value is especially high when moving data, rather than performing arithmetic, limits useful work.

items.p: A new AI processor uses non-HBM memory. What follows for assessing an HBM control?
keys: Its effect depends on the design and workload
items.x: Epoch describes Huawei variants using LPDDR and Nvidia products using GDDR memory. HBM can be a major constraint without being universal to every AI chip.
items.answer: Its effect depends on the design and workload

o: Its effect depends on the design and workload
The processor cannot perform AI inference
The control necessarily prevents every unit from being built
The memory choice removes all other export requirements
ow: AI accelerators can use other memory, with different tradeoffs.
Non-HBM variants can avoid this particular input constraint.
Other item, destination and end-user rules remain relevant.

items.p: Which group contains the three established leading HBM suppliers?
o: SK hynix, Samsung and Micron
TSMC, Intel and Samsung
SK hynix, TSMC and CXMT
Micron, ASML and Tokyo Electron
ow: TSMC is a major foundry and packager; Intel is not one of the three established leading HBM suppliers.
TSMC packages processors with HBM, while CXMT is an emerging Chinese memory producer.
ASML and Tokyo Electron make semiconductor-manufacturing tools, rather than HBM.
keys: SK hynix, Samsung and Micron
items.x: The major established suppliers are SK hynix, Samsung and Micron. Nvidia lists all three as memory suppliers; Epoch identifies them as the main HBM producers. Supplier concentration is different from proving that memory is the binding constraint for a particular design.

items.p: Match each constraint to the production question it raises.
pairs: Can enough usable processor dies be made?
Can enough suitable high-bandwidth memory be supplied?
Can dies and memory be joined in the required package?
Can processors exchange data efficiently in the larger system?
items.x: Adding wafer capacity solves only one part of the map. Product design, memory, packaging and connections determine the usable system.

items.p: Why can HBM availability cap output even when a manufacturer has finished logic dies?
keys: An HBM-based product needs both inputs to ship
items.x: For a design built around HBM, unused logic dies do not become finished accelerators by themselves. Alternative designs can ease a constraint while changing performance tradeoffs.
items.answer: An HBM-based product needs both inputs to ship

o: An HBM-based product needs both inputs to ship
More logic dies can be substituted for each missing memory stack
A chip license guarantees that memory suppliers reserve capacity
The memory can always be fitted later without package redesign
ow: Logic computation and memory supply are different functions.
A license does not establish capacity or a supply contract.
Package designs and memory interfaces constrain substitution.

units.title: What makes a chip controlled
units.desc: Separate technical classification, jurisdiction and transaction-specific licensing. Then examine thresholds and design responses.

items.p: Match each export-control question to what it establishes.
pairs: Is the item subject to the EAR?
Whether this US regulatory system reaches the item
Which technical control entry describes it
Who receives it and for what use?
Whether a license or exception permits the transaction
items.x: A technical threshold is one step in a compliance analysis. Being subject to the EAR is not itself a conclusion that every transaction requires a license.

items.p: Match each export-control code or designation to its role.
pairs: Specified advanced-computing chips and certain HBM
Specified computers and assemblies containing controlled chips
An EAR-subject item not specified on the Commerce Control List
items.x: A code identifies an item category; it does not by itself settle every license requirement. EAR99 items can still require authorization because of destination, end-user or end-use restrictions.

items.p: A chip falls below one advanced-computing threshold. Why is license-free export not yet established?
o: Other item, end-use or end-user controls may apply
The threshold automatically changes with the buyer's budget
Below-threshold chips are all designated EAR99
A manufacturer can waive federal controls by changing the model name
ow: Buyer budgets do not alter the technical definition.
Failing one threshold does not settle the full classification.
Product names do not supply authority to waive controls.
keys: Other item, end-use or end-user controls may apply
items.x: Classification, destination and parties all matter. Screening only a headline processing number can miss another controlled tier or a separate restriction.

items.p: A chip has TPP 4,000 and performance density 6.5. Under the October 2023 3A090.a tests, which result follows?
o: It meets the combined TPP-and-density route
It fails because its TPP is below 4,800
It qualifies only if the customer is military
It fails because density applies only above TPP 4,800
ow: The entry also covers TPP of at least 1,600 with density of at least 5.92.
The technical classification is distinct from later end-use analysis.
The combined route specifically reaches some chips below TPP 4,800.
keys: It meets the combined TPP-and-density route
items.x: The hypothetical chip clears 1,600 TPP and 5.92 density. This teaches the two alternative routes into that entry, rather than treating 4,800 as its only test.

items.p: Why can defining controlled chips by performance reduce dependence on product names?
keys: Comparable new products can meet the same criteria
items.x: Vendor-neutral parameters can cover comparable products. They also invite designs near the boundary, so their relationship to useful capability requires review.
items.answer: Comparable new products can meet the same criteria

o: Comparable new products can meet the same criteria
Every future chip becomes controlled without regard to capability
Only the vendor used to develop the thresholds is covered
A chip automatically leaves control once its brand is renamed
ow: Technical criteria still distinguish products by their parameters.
The criteria can apply across vendors.
Renaming does not change a product's technical characteristics.

items.p: Under the 2023 rule, why should a reviewer avoid comparing chip speeds quoted at different bit precisions without adjustment?
o: The legal metric incorporates operation bit length
Only the fastest advertised operations count, regardless of precision
All 8-bit operations are excluded from processing performance
A precision label establishes the memory bandwidth automatically
ow: The rule specifies how performance and bit length enter TPP.
The technical note explicitly gives an 8-bit example.
Arithmetic precision and memory bandwidth are different properties.
keys: The legal metric incorporates operation bit length
items.x: The rule defines TPP using twice MacTOPS times operation bit length, with instructions on aggregation, maximum precision-mode values and dense computation. Marketing FLOPS alone are insufficient.

items.p: What workaround did BIS say its 2023 performance-density test targeted?
keys: Combining many small, dense chips below a total-performance line
items.x: A total-performance threshold alone can leave smaller chips useful in aggregate. Density adds processing per area to the classification, although it is still a proxy.
items.answer: Combining many small, dense chips below a total-performance line

o: Combining many small, dense chips below a total-performance line
Concealing a controlled chip inside a computer server
Shipping through an intermediary with misleading paperwork
Obtaining a license under an invented company name
ow: Servers containing controlled chips have their own control entries.
Diversion and false paperwork require enforcement and party checks.
Identity deception is separate from the technical density parameter.

items.p: Nvidia disclosed an April 2025 license requirement for the H20 and chips reaching its memory bandwidth. What lesson does the disclosure illustrate?
o: A compute-focused line can leave memory-related capability important
Bit-precision rules automatically capture every memory-bandwidth risk
Every below-threshold product is permanently exempt from later controls
A company disclosure changes the regulation for all destinations
ow: Arithmetic precision and memory movement measure different constraints.
Requirements can change, including through notified controls.
The disclosure reports a US government requirement with specified scope.
keys: A compute-focused line can leave memory-related capability important
items.x: Nvidia's filing identifies a bandwidth-related trigger. A design optimized around one legal line can remain useful along another performance dimension.

items.p: Why must a reviewer distinguish standalone HBM from a processor package containing HBM?
keys: The relevant control entries treat those forms differently
items.x: The December 2024 HBM entry has a note concerning co-packaged items whose dominant function is processing. The completed processor may still be controlled under another entry.
items.answer: The relevant control entries treat those forms differently

o: The relevant control entries treat those forms differently
HBM loses its physical bandwidth when packaged with a processor
Memory made abroad is exempt whenever a US designer packages it
Packaging replaces technical classification with the retail price
ow: Packaging does not make the memory cease to provide bandwidth.
Jurisdiction and applicable entries still need to be checked.
Retail price is not a substitute for the entry's technical tests.

units.title: Reaching foreign production and foreign buyers
units.desc: Apply foreign-product rules, customer verification and ownership-related controls without treating every connection as a blanket ban.

items.p: A chip contains little controlled US content but was produced with covered technology. Which separate route could bring it under the EAR?
o: An applicable foreign-direct product rule
The chip designer's choice of its retail brand
An automatic rule covering every foreign-made semiconductor
A rule that treats all foreign production as US-origin
ow: A brand does not establish jurisdiction.
FDP rules have defined product and destination or end-user scope.
Covered foreign-made items do not simply become US-origin.
keys: An applicable foreign-direct product rule
items.x: De minimis rules concern incorporated controlled content. FDP rules can reach specified foreign-produced items through their production technology, when the full conditions are met.

items.p: An FDP rule makes a foreign-produced item subject to the EAR. What must the exporter determine next?
o: The licensing requirements for the particular transaction
Whether subject-to-EAR status itself grants a general export license
Whether every customer worldwide is now prohibited
Whether its retail price exceeds a statutory cap
ow: Jurisdiction does not supply authorization; the applicable transaction still needs analysis.
Not every transaction involving an EAR-subject item requires a license.
A price cap is not the next general jurisdictional test.
keys: The licensing requirements for the particular transaction
items.x: The regulation explicitly separates EAR jurisdiction from license requirements and possible exceptions. Keep the map of classification, recipient and use in view.

items.p: Why did BIS add foundry due-diligence measures for advanced chips in January 2025?

Every advanced chip is destined for a prohibited military user
Foundries lack any ability to identify who ordered fabrication
The foundry should choose geopolitical policy instead of following rules
ow: Advanced technical capability does not establish prohibited intent.
Foundries have customer information; verifying its adequacy is the issue.
Due diligence implements defined requirements rather than unfettered policy choice.

items.x: The rule establishes presumptions for front-end fabricators and packaging firms, with specified ways to overcome them. It addresses the risk of misleading customers and inaccurate classification.

items.p: A foundry cannot overcome an applicable advanced-chip classification presumption. What follows?
keys: It must apply the resulting licensing requirements
items.x: The January 2025 rule tells covered fabricators and packaging firms to comply with applicable 3A090.a requirements unless an allowed route overcomes the presumption. It does not make every destination an automatic denial.
items.answer: It must apply the resulting licensing requirements

o: It must apply the resulting licensing requirements
It must reject every order regardless of the destination
Its customer can cancel the presumption by changing the brand
The presumption establishes that an export crime has occurred
ow: A requirement may allow a license or another authorized route.
A brand change does not supply the required evidence.
A presumption governing compliance is not a criminal conviction.

items.p: A China-headquartered firm's subsidiary in Malaysia orders covered advanced computing items. Does Malaysia's location alone settle the license requirement?
o: No, the headquarters-related requirement can still apply
Yes, buyer ownership never matters outside China
Yes, unless the subsidiary is individually on the Entity List
No, because every shipment of electronics to Malaysia is banned
ow: BIS guidance specifically addresses relevant entities outside the restricted destination.
The headquarters requirement does not depend solely on an individual listing.
The requirement concerns specified items and recipients, rather than all electronics.
keys: No, the headquarters-related requirement can still apply
items.x: BIS's May 31, 2026 guidance restates the requirement for entities headquartered in D:5 or Macau, or with an ultimate parent headquartered there. Check the covered items and transaction.

items.p: How does an Entity List entry differ from a license-review policy?
keys: One establishes restrictions; the other guides review of applications
items.x: Read the entry's covered items and licensing policy separately. A listing need not imply the same treatment for every item or the absence of any licensing route.
items.answer: One establishes restrictions; the other guides review of applications

o: One establishes restrictions; the other guides review of applications
The entry bans every financial transaction with the named entity
The review policy determines whether an item is physically made in the US
An entry and a presumption of denial mean precisely the same thing
ow: The Entity List is an export-control instrument, rather than a universal financial block.
Review policy concerns license decisions, not manufacturing geography.
Entries can carry different scopes and review policies.

items.p: What mechanism did BIS's September 2025 affiliates rule introduce?
o: Extending specified restrictions through qualifying listed-entity ownership
Licensing every cloud session involving a Chinese customer
Treating any US-made tool as sufficient to prohibit all factory output
Controlling all firms with even one employee formerly at a listed company
ow: The rule concerns ownership-related restrictions, rather than every cloud service.
Product-rule jurisdiction has separate conditions.
The stated ownership test is not a former-employee test.
keys: Extending specified restrictions through qualifying listed-entity ownership
items.x: The rule uses an at-least-50% ownership test, including defined aggregation and indirect ownership. A November 2025 notice suspended it; do not confuse knowing its mechanism with knowing its current effective status.

items.p: A company cites a press statement extending a trade truce. What should counsel check before relying on a delayed affiliates-rule restart?
keys: The operative suspension notice and any subsequent legal changes
items.x: The November 2025 notice schedules reimposition on November 10, 2026. This historical notice is not proof that no later change exists; check the operative instruments for the transaction date.
items.answer: The operative suspension notice and any subsequent legal changes

o: The operative suspension notice and any subsequent legal changes
Whether the press statement received more coverage than the regulation
Whether the company's distributor has renamed its subsidiaries
Whether a tariff delay automatically suspends every export control
ow: Media prominence does not determine which legal text governs.
A rename does not establish a legal suspension.
Tariffs and export-control requirements have separate legal mechanisms.

units.title: Licenses, policy shifts and allies
units.desc: Read the January 2026 H200 policy and July UAE rule, separating permissions, conditions, tariffs and enforcement choices.

items.p: The January 2026 H200-class rule changed certain China-bound license reviews. What changed?
o: Some qualifying applications moved to case-by-case review
The listed chips became license-free for all Chinese buyers
Every chip below Nvidia's newest model received automatic approval
The rule removed the need to check end users and end uses
ow: The rule changed review policy while retaining licenses and conditions.
Eligibility uses specified criteria rather than a simple product-generation ranking.
End-user and end-use restrictions remain relevant.
keys: Some qualifying applications moved to case-by-case review
items.x: The rule covers qualifying exports from the US to China or Macau, with performance and other conditions. A review route is not an issued license or evidence that a shipment occurred.

items.p: A chip has TPP 18,000 and total DRAM bandwidth 8,000 GB/s. Does it meet the January 2026 policy's paired performance ceilings?
o: No, its bandwidth exceeds the stated ceiling
Yes, its TPP is below 21,000
Yes, if it was commercially available in the United States
No, every chip above TPP 4,800 is excluded from case-by-case review
ow: The policy also requires total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s.
US commercial availability is another condition, not a substitute for the ceilings.
The January policy permits some chips above the earlier classification threshold.
keys: No, its bandwidth exceeds the stated ceiling
items.x: The hypothetical fails the bandwidth condition despite meeting the TPP condition. Classification thresholds and conditions for a licensing-policy route answer different questions.

items.p: Which January 2026 H200-policy condition relates directly to supply for US customers?
o: China and Macau shipments are capped relative to US end-use shipments
Each China sale requires delivery of a newer generation to a US buyer
Only government orders receive priority over Chinese customers
US customers must match the price offered by foreign buyers
ow: The rule uses supply and shipment conditions, rather than a matching newer-product sale.
Its supply conditions are not limited to government purchasers.
A customer price-matching rule is not the stated condition.
keys: China and Macau shipments are capped relative to US end-use shipments
items.x: The stated aggregate cap is 50% of the same product shipped for US end use. The applicant must also address US supply and non-diversion of relevant foundry capacity.

items.p: Why does eligibility for case-by-case review fail to establish that an H200 shipment to China can occur?
keys: A license and other applicable conditions still need to be satisfied
items.x: Return to the map: classification, authorization and physical delivery are different steps. This distinction prevents policy announcements from being mistaken for completed sales.
items.answer: A license and other applicable conditions still need to be satisfied

o: A license and other applicable conditions still need to be satisfied
Eligibility automatically supplies approval by the importing country
The performance ceilings are suggestions with no licensing role
A public announcement replaces all shipment-level documentation
ow: US eligibility cannot establish a foreign government's import permission.
The ceilings help define eligibility for this review policy.
Public announcements do not replace applicable legal and documentary requirements.

items.p: How did the administration describe collecting its 25% H200-related payment in early 2026?
o: Through an import tariff when chips enter the US for testing
As a BIS application fee paid for each export-license request
As a tax collected by Chinese customs for the US Treasury
As an automatic deduction from every semiconductor company's profits
ow: CRS distinguishes the described tariff from a prohibited export-license fee.
The collection point described is US importation.
The arrangement is not a general corporate-profits tax.
keys: Through an import tariff when chips enter the US for testing
items.x: CRS reports the administration's explanation and identifies legal uncertainties. The tariff proclamation and the export-license policy are separate instruments; the course does not assume a court has upheld the arrangement.

items.p: BIS's July 2026 UAE rule describes selective non-enforcement of the Diffusion rule. What does that teach about reading regulatory status?
keys: Written requirements and enforcement policy can diverge
items.x: Use the dated July rule as evidence of the distinction. It described enforcement limited to certain country groups and covered headquarters cases, rather than treating the 2025 announcement as universal deregulation.
items.answer: Written requirements and enforcement policy can diverge

o: Written requirements and enforcement policy can diverge
An announced rescission necessarily removes all regulatory text immediately
A non-enforcement decision repeals every older headquarters restriction
The status of one rule determines whether all Gulf buyers are approved
ow: Formal text and enforcement statements can change through different actions.
BIS's May guidance explicitly maintains the earlier headquarters requirement.
Recipient-specific rules still require separate analysis.

items.p: Under the July 2026 UAE rule, why is "the UAE can buy chips freely" too broad?
o: Favorable treatment depends on qualifying recipients and remaining controls
Country Group A:5 membership prohibits every commercial chip purchase
The country-group change authorizes every company operating in the UAE
Every company operating in the UAE becomes a US-headquartered entity
ow: The rule expands certain favorable treatment.
The rule preserves requirements outside its specified government and approved-recipient routes.
Operating in a country does not change a company's headquarters.
keys: Favorable treatment depends on qualifying recipients and remaining controls
items.x: The rule preserves advanced-computing license requirements except for specified government and approved commercial or US-headquartered recipients and relevant subsidiaries. End-use and other controls remain.

items.p: Match each policy instrument to what it changes.
pairs: Which item characteristics fall within a classification
How covered license applications are assessed
Which transaction or recipients can use a permission
How an agency says it will apply specified requirements
items.x: A tariff is another instrument still: it governs duties on imports, rather than replacing export authorization. Always identify which step a new announcement actually changes.

units.title: Diversion, remote access and verification
units.desc: Distinguish observed violations from estimated flows, and a chip's location from the identity of the person using it.

items.p: In a March 2026 indictment, how did prosecutors allege a server-diversion scheme misled inspections?
o: By staging dummy servers for inspection
By obtaining an exception that legalized the China destination
By moving the computing workload while leaving every server in place
By securing a court order replacing export licenses
ow: The indictment alleges evasion rather than authorized delivery.
The alleged scheme involved physical server diversion.
A court order supplying such export permission is not the alleged mechanism.
keys: By staging dummy servers for inspection
items.x: The Justice Department alleges dummy equipment and deceptive logistics. Charges are allegations, not findings of guilt; an inspection can be misled if equipment identity and records are not corroborated.

items.p: Why can a legitimate first sale fail to establish a server's final destination?
o: Resale or onward shipment can change who receives it
The first buyer automatically transfers its export license to any later purchaser
Once sold abroad, an EAR-subject item exits all US jurisdiction
Installing a controlled chip in a server removes its classification
ow: Authorization does not automatically cover arbitrary onward transfers.
Reexport and in-country transfer rules can still apply.
Computers and servers can have their own applicable entries.
keys: Resale or onward shipment can change who receives it
items.x: The alleged diversion case separates a declared intermediary from later recipients. Compliance needs transaction and destination evidence beyond the first invoice.

items.p: Why are estimates of undetected chip smuggling sensitive to assumptions?
keys: Observed cases must be extrapolated to unobserved flows
items.x: Epoch's smuggling analysis models uncertainty around observed activity. A range depends partly on assumptions about the fraction detected, so do not present it as a census.
items.answer: Observed cases must be extrapolated to unobserved flows

o: Observed cases must be extrapolated to unobserved flows
Every server seizure is counted as a whole year of legal exports
The estimates can directly observe transactions that escaped detection
A higher number of press reports mechanically proves higher total diversion
ow: A seizure count and a legal-export total are distinct quantities.
Undetected flows are inferred rather than directly counted.
Reporting intensity and detection can change independently of total diversion.

items.p: Three reports give similar smuggling estimates. Which check best tests whether this is independent corroboration?
o: Whether their data, authors and models overlap
Whether the totals use the same performance units
Whether their headline totals cover the same year
Whether each publication passed an editorial review
ow: Common units support comparability, rather than showing that the evidence is independent.
A common period helps comparison, rather than establishing separate data or methods.
Editorial review may improve quality without making shared underlying evidence independent.
keys: Whether their data, authors and models overlap
items.x: Trace the underlying evidence. Reports can repeat or adapt the same model; agreement then contributes less new information than three independent measurements.

lessons.title: Where the chip is, and who uses it

items.p: A rented accelerator stays in an overseas data center while a user accesses it from China. What gap does this illustrate?
o: Controlling physical shipments differs from controlling use of compute services
The accelerator necessarily becomes physically located in China
All cloud services automatically export the underlying chip to the user
A lawful chip location establishes that every remote use is authorized
ow: A remote user does not physically move the chip.
A service transaction and shipment are distinct regulatory questions.
User identity, end use and other obligations can still matter.
keys: Controlling physical shipments differs from controlling use of compute services
items.x: CSET describes the service-versus-item distinction. Do not turn it into a blanket claim of legality: applicable end-use restrictions, license conditions and other laws still need review.

items.p: Why might a successful chip-location check leave restricted remote use undetected?
keys: The chip may be at the approved site while its user is elsewhere
items.x: Retrieve two checkpoints: location verification addresses physical diversion; customer and access controls address who uses the capacity. Neither supplies the other automatically.
items.answer: The chip may be at the approved site while its user is elsewhere

o: The chip may be at the approved site while its user is elsewhere
A location check automatically identifies every account holder
A chip can only answer a location check from its purchaser's country
Remote access always requires physically moving the memory stacks
ow: Location evidence is not user-identity evidence.
The check concerns the chip's location, not a purchaser's legal domicile.
Remote use can occur while the hardware remains stationary.

items.p: What does a very fast authenticated reply to a trusted landmark support in delay-based location verification?
o: An upper bound on the chip's distance from that landmark
A precise street address independent of network conditions
Proof that the current user has an approved institutional affiliation
A command giving the government access to model weights
ow: Latency and implementation assumptions limit geographic precision.
A timing measurement does not verify institutional identity.
The proposed location check is distinct from reading workloads or weights.
keys: An upper bound on the chip's distance from that landmark
items.x: IAPS describes authenticated timing as evidence of a maximum plausible distance. Delays can make a reply slower, so a slow response alone does not prove the chip is far away.

items.p: Why should location verification be distinguished from remote disabling?
keys: Reporting location and preventing operation are different capabilities
items.x: IAPS distinguishes verification from geofencing that would disable a chip. A policy assessment should specify what hardware reports, who receives it and what enforcement follows.
items.answer: Reporting location and preventing operation are different capabilities

o: Reporting location and preventing operation are different capabilities
Every signed location reply already shuts down the processor
A chip must disclose workload contents to establish approximate location
A location proposal automatically becomes a legal requirement
ow: Reporting does not itself establish a shutdown mechanism.
The proposal describes a signed timing exchange rather than workload inspection.
A technical proposal and an operative legal duty are different.

units.title: China's domestic production and adaptation
units.desc: Assess manufacturing milestones, memory constraints and system strategies without treating forecasts or roadmaps as delivered output.

items.p: Huawei announces a system linking many Ascend chips. What should a reviewer compare with a rival system?
o: Delivered workload performance, resources and usable scale
The number of chips alone, regardless of their capabilities
The planned rack count as proof of already completed deliveries
The designer's nationality as a sufficient performance measure
ow: Chip counts omit per-chip performance and system overheads.
A roadmap is not a shipment record.
Nationality does not measure effective workload performance.
keys: Delivered workload performance, resources and usable scale
items.x: Huawei's 2025 announcement emphasizes large connected systems. Attribute its performance claims and check independent measurements and delivered scale before treating a roadmap as achieved parity.

items.p: Why does linking more processors not eliminate every disadvantage of weaker individual chips?
keys: Communication, power and supply needs can rise with scale
items.x: System design can trade more hardware and interconnect for performance. Compare practical throughput and resource needs instead of inferring parity from a processor count.
items.answer: Communication, power and supply needs can rise with scale

o: Communication, power and supply needs can rise with scale
A larger system necessarily uses fewer memory components
Interconnect makes the physical number of available chips irrelevant
Software removes the need for the chips to exchange data
ow: More processors do not inherently reduce component needs.
Available hardware still limits how large a system can be.
Distributed workloads still require communication.

items.p: Epoch forecasts Huawei production from domestic memory supply. Which statement accurately characterizes that result?
o: A modeled outcome conditional on supply and yield assumptions
An audited count of every chip Huawei has already shipped
A government guarantee that the roadmap will be completed
Proof that alternative non-HBM designs cannot matter
ow: A production forecast is distinct from shipment records.
An analyst model is not a state guarantee.
The analysis explicitly discusses alternative memory and workload tradeoffs.
keys: A modeled outcome conditional on supply and yield assumptions
items.x: Epoch models HBM wafer allocation, yields, allocation to Huawei and production lags. Changes to those assumptions can materially change the forecast.

items.p: A new control targets an input for which firms already hold inventories. Why might output initially continue?
o: Stocks can bridge the gap before replacement supply is needed
The control automatically legalizes all future input purchases
An inventory buffer proves the targeted input is unnecessary
A delayed effect establishes that domestic substitutes are already equivalent
ow: Prior stock does not authorize later prohibited transactions.
Using stock can show dependence rather than irrelevance.
Inventories can explain a delay without demonstrating substitute performance.
keys: Stocks can bridge the gap before replacement supply is needed
items.x: Distinguish a flow restriction from the stock already available. Epoch's memory analysis illustrates why near-term output alone may not reveal a control's longer-term effect.

units.title: Put the physical and legal maps together
units.desc: Interleave product design, jurisdiction, licensing, supply and evidence quality in practical review scenarios.

items.p: A firm says its foreign-made chip falls outside the EAR because it contains little US content. What is the best next check?
o: Whether an applicable FDP rule reaches its production
Whether a new brand name can replace a jurisdiction review
Whether foreign manufacture exempts all related software
Whether the first sale has already occurred
ow: A new brand does not alter the jurisdictional conditions.
Software and technology can have their own controls.
A prior sale does not settle later jurisdiction or restrictions.
keys: Whether an applicable FDP rule reaches its production
items.x: Reuse the distinction between incorporated content and production technology. Then assess classification, recipients, destination and authorization if jurisdiction applies.

items.p: An unvetted startup orders an advanced die from a foundry. What would make "it is not on the Entity List" an incomplete answer?
o: Foundry presumptions and other controls can apply independently
Every unlisted startup is automatically a prohibited end user
A foundry can disregard classification for new customers
All orders below a chosen dollar amount are exempt
ow: Unlisted status does not automatically establish prohibition either.
The due-diligence rule applies defined criteria to covered orders.
A purchase-price exemption is not the general rule established here.
keys: Foundry presumptions and other controls can apply independently
items.x: The January 2025 due-diligence measures require more than a list search. The April 2026 notice extended a designer-status deadline, illustrating why implementation dates also need checking.

items.p: BIS declines to enforce new Diffusion-rule requirements. Why can a China-headquartered firm's foreign subsidiary still need a license for covered advanced chips?
o: The earlier headquarters-related requirement can remain
Only the physical location of the server determines licensing
The Diffusion country caps return under a new name automatically
A voluntary promise by chip designers supplies the legal requirement
ow: BIS guidance addresses headquarters and ultimate-parent headquarters even for entities abroad.
The reason is an earlier requirement, rather than an automatically renamed country cap.
The relevant duty comes from the export rules, as clarified by BIS guidance.
keys: The earlier headquarters-related requirement can remain
items.x: The guidance expressly says the preexisting headquarters requirement continues to be enforced. Distinguish the new requirements subject to non-enforcement from older restrictions.

items.p: A shipment meets the H200 policy's performance ceilings. Why should an exporter still review the recipient's remote-access controls?
keys: The policy includes conditions addressing unauthorized access
items.x: The January 2026 rule includes KYC-related commitments against unauthorized remote access. Product eligibility and customer controls address different parts of the transaction.
items.answer: The policy includes conditions addressing unauthorized access

o: The policy includes conditions addressing unauthorized access
Memory bandwidth alone authenticates all remote users
A case-by-case review eliminates all customer due diligence
An overseas customer cannot grant anyone remote use
ow: A bandwidth specification provides no identity verification.
The review policy includes customer and security conditions.
An overseas operator may provide remote access, which makes controls relevant.

items.p: A proposal lowers only a compute threshold. What should its drafter examine using the H20 lesson?
o: Useful capability that depends on memory bandwidth
Whether a new threshold automatically bans all foreign cloud services
Whether below-threshold chips must be obsolete in every workload
Whether new model names can replace technical specifications
ow: A chip threshold does not by itself define control over all services.
A restricted processing rate can coexist with useful performance on some tasks.
Model names do not replace technical evidence.
keys: Useful capability that depends on memory bandwidth
items.x: A good proxy tracks the intended restriction across plausible designs and workloads. Nvidia's April 2025 disclosure shows why memory characteristics can matter alongside compute.

items.p: A government funds domestic logic fabs but leaves memory and packaging unexamined. Which question best tests the plan?
o: Which remaining stage limits finished systems?
How much of the fabrication subsidy has already been spent
How many processor designs received domestic development grants
Whether the new fab uses the newest advertised process node
ow: Spending measures implementation activity; it does not identify the remaining limit on completed systems.
A design count does not establish sufficient fabrication, memory or packaging capacity.
An advanced node can improve logic dies while leaving memory or packaging as the production bottleneck.
keys: Which remaining stage limits finished systems?
items.x: Return to the first map: successful domestic fabrication does not automatically supply suitable memory or advanced packaging. Assess complete products and their required inputs.

items.p: A press release reports "one million AI chips smuggled". Which check is most important before repeating it?
o: Whether it is observed or modeled, and what its units mean
Whether the chips were the latest commercial generation
Whether one seized shipment was traced to its manufacturer
Whether legal chip imports fell during the same period
ow: Generation matters to capability, but first establish whether the headline is a count, estimate or compute-equivalent measure.
Tracing one shipment supports a case; it does not validate the estimated total in the press release.
Legal imports provide context, but do not establish the statistic's provenance, units or uncertainty.
keys: Whether it is observed or modeled, and what its units mean
