items.x: This is a hypothesized reinforcing loop, rather than evidence that it already causes an explosion. Its strength depends on how much better AI increases research output and how efficiently new ideas become useful models.

items.p: In Forethought's simplified fixed-hardware feedback model, r measures software doublings per doubling of cumulative research effort. Under its other assumptions, which r produces faster successive doublings?
o: r greater than 1
Any r greater than 0
r exactly equal to 1
r less than 1
ow: Positive returns alone need not overcome diminishing returns to research.
In the simplified model, r equal to 1 gives constant exponential growth.
In the simplified model, r below 1 gives progressively slower doublings.
keys: r greater than 1
items.x: This is a model-conditional threshold. It assumes software improvements increase effective AI research output in the specified way and ignores some limits, including parallelization. Empirical training-efficiency gains alone do not establish the relevant r for autonomous research.

items.p: Why can a fixed experiment-compute budget limit the speedup from adding many AI researchers?
items.answer: If experiments require scarce compute, faster idea generation can leave researchers waiting for tests. The effect depends on how well more cognitive labor can substitute for compute.
keys: experiments use scarce compute
labor-compute substitutability determines the limit

choice.p: Why can a fixed experiment-compute budget limit the speedup from adding many AI researchers?
o: Compute-heavy experiments can limit the value of additional research labor
Extra research labor automatically creates the chips needed to test its ideas
More AI researchers make every experiment finish proportionally faster
Any compute bottleneck rules out all further algorithmic improvements
ow: Research software can improve efficiency, but extra labor does not automatically add hardware.
Some experiment costs cannot be reduced simply by adding researchers.
Bottlenecks can limit acceleration without stopping every improvement.

items.x: Whitfill and Wu fit two models to data on four labs and obtained different conclusions about substitution. Davidson argues bottlenecks may bind late. The crux is how much acceleration survives the constraint, rather than a choice between infinite acceleration and a single one-off gain.

items.p: Match each position on AI research automation to the argument its authors make.
pairs: Software feedback could overcome diminishing returns and drive an explosion
Experimental compute and real-world data make a software-only explosion doubtful
Current agents' failures on open-ended research limit what narrow benchmarks establish
Acceleration depends on the strength of several uncertain feedback relationships
items.x: These are attributed arguments, rather than settled forecasts. Current task failures constrain evidence for present capabilities without proving a permanent limit; a feedback model likewise needs empirical support for its assumptions.

lessons.title: Measure the effect, not a proxy

items.p: In Epoch's October 2026 InnovationEval pilot, two tested models tried to reinvent a recent post-training innovation. What did the in-scope results show?
o: Both fell short of matching the human innovation
Both reproduced the full improvement by a different route
One clearly exceeded the human result after scope checks
Neither produced any measured gain on any part of the task
ow: The tested methods fell short of the original innovation's gains.
Reported gains required scope review, and neither matched the human result.
One model achieved partial in-scope gains, so zero improvement is too strong.
keys: both tested models fell short on the in-scope research task
items.x: Epoch tested Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Sol achieved partial gains after scope and time-cost adjustments; Fable's apparent gains were excluded as out of scope. This small pilot tests a specific research task, rather than establishing that models cannot contribute useful research.

items.p: Match each research-automation measure to the quantity it measures.
pairs: How much work is classified as mostly performed by AI
How much agent execution occurs relative to human working time
How much faster or more productive an assisted worker is
How much faster capability progress occurs because of AI
items.x: Anthropic's automation index and OpenAI's runtime statistics illustrate the first two measures. Neither is an overall acceleration estimate. METR proposes examining multiple evidence sources and alternative explanations to estimate the final quantity.

items.p: Anthropic reported in August 2026 that Claude led 26% of its AI research work. What additional question is needed before converting that into a speedup estimate?
o: Net time savings after supervision and other constraints
Whether the percentage can be added to a model's benchmark accuracy
Whether 26% is above a universal threshold for autonomous research
How many tasks can be renamed to put more work in the AI-led category
ow: A task share and benchmark accuracy measure different things.
There is no universal threshold that converts a task share into autonomous research.
Reclassification can change a statistic without changing productive output.
keys: Net time savings after supervision and other constraints
items.x: Anthropic classifies work using its own models and notes obstacles to cross-lab comparison. Its reported share concerns the tasks measured, rather than a claim that all research is 26% faster. Staff-time weighting and supervision affect interpretation.

items.p: Why should a forecast based on workers' self-reported AI speedups be checked against observed outcomes?
items.answer: People can misjudge how AI changes task time. Direct measurement can reveal a different effect, while study samples may also differ from the workers being forecast.
keys: self-assessed speedups can differ from measured task times
check applicability of the measurement setting

choice.p: Why should a forecast based on workers' self-reported AI speedups be checked against observed outcomes?
o: Perceived benefits can differ from measured effects on task completion
Self-reports measure the unobserved no-AI counterfactual directly
Random assignment automatically makes a study representative of every workplace
A positive self-report proves that all assistance tasks were performed correctly
ow: Workers cannot directly observe both versions of the same completed task.
Randomization supports causal inference within the study, rather than universal representativeness.
Perceived speed does not establish work quality or net time savings.

items.x: METR's early-2025 trial found a slowdown among experienced open-source developers despite perceived speedups. Its later study faced selection and measurement problems. Both surveys and trials need scrutiny before extrapolating to internal AI research.

items.p: A lab's capability progress accelerates after it adopts more AI researchers and doubles experiment compute. What should an assessor do before attributing the acceleration to AI?
o: Separate AI assistance from compute changes using several lines of evidence
Attribute all above-trend progress to whichever input changed most recently
Treat the lab's total code output as a direct measure of progress
Ignore internal evidence because only released models can be assessed
ow: Changes can coincide; timing alone does not isolate a cause.
Code output is a proxy that can rise without a proportional research gain.
An assessor with access can investigate unreleased models and internal processes.
keys: Separate AI assistance from compute changes using several lines of evidence
items.x: METR's October 2026 proposal separates measuring acceleration from explaining it. The no-AI counterfactual is unobserved, so capability trends, input growth, workflow evidence and bottlenecks must be considered together.

units.title: Reading trends: rates, bends and ceilings
units.desc: Practice the arithmetic, then test how much the forecast depends on its fit, measurement range and assumed link to real work.

items.p: Hypothetical: two fits give doubling times of 7 months and 4 months. Over the next 24 months, how much growth would each imply if it held?
o: About 11x and 64x, respectively
About 3x and 6x, respectively
About 3x and 8x, respectively
About 22x and 128x, respectively
ow: Growth is 2 raised to the number of doublings, rather than the number of doublings itself.
These factors understate exponential growth over the full period.
This adds an extra doubling to both calculations.
keys: about 11-fold at seven months and 64-fold at four months
items.x: Compute 2^(24/7), about 10.8, and 2^(24/4), which is 64. METR's January 2026 fits differed by time window; its post-2023 figure was about 131 days, rather than exactly four months. A rounded rate can materially change a long extrapolation.

items.p: Hypothetical: a 50% task horizon is 10 human-work hours and doubles every four months. What does a constant-rate extrapolation give for reaching 160 hours?
o: 16 months: four doublings
8 months: two doublings
24 months: six doublings
60 months: adding ten hours every four months
ow: Two doublings reach 40 hours.
Six doublings reach 640 hours.
A doubling trend multiplies the quantity rather than adding a fixed amount.
keys: four doublings take sixteen months
items.x: The sequence is 10, 20, 40, 80, 160. This is an arithmetic implication of an assumed trend. It does not show that the measurement can support such horizons or that a 50% success rate would suffice for real projects.

items.p: A simple uplift model starts at 2x coding speed, doubles the extra speedup (uplift minus 1) every five months, and defines its target as 20x. About how long does reaching the target take?
o: 21 months, because the extra speedup must grow from 1 to 19
17 months, because the total speedup must grow from 2 to 20
95 months, because the extra speedup needs nineteen doublings
5 months, because doubling a speedup reaches the target
ow: This extrapolates total uplift, rather than the specified quantity uplift minus 1.
A 19-fold rise needs log2(19), about 4.25, doublings.
One doubling of the extra speedup produces 3x total uplift.
keys: about 21 months from 5 times log2(19)
items.x: Five times log2(19) is about 21.2 months. These are median parameter choices in the AI Futures Project's August 2026 illustrative model. Substituting median inputs into a nonlinear model need not produce the median of its full forecast distribution.

items.p: Why can several curves fit past capability measurements well and still imply very different arrival dates?
items.answer: The observed data may not distinguish their shapes. Extrapolation magnifies differences between exponential, accelerating and slowing growth.
keys: historical fit can underdetermine curve shape
different shapes diverge outside the observed range

choice.p: Why can several curves fit past capability measurements well and still imply very different arrival dates?
o: Similar historical fit can hide sharply different out-of-sample growth
The curve with the most parameters necessarily predicts the future best
A close fit establishes the same causal mechanism will continue
Discarding older points removes uncertainty about future curve shape
ow: Extra flexibility can improve fit without improving prediction.
A statistical fit does not establish a stable causal mechanism.
A shorter window can change the estimate without resolving the underlying uncertainty.

items.x: Titotal criticized the sensitivity of AI 2027's extrapolations; the authors disputed much of the critique and acknowledged errors. The practical response is sensitivity analysis and explicit assumptions, rather than treating a fitted curve as a law.

items.p: Match each uncertainty in a timeline extrapolation to a useful check.
pairs: Compare constant, accelerating and slowing fits
Test power, financing, hardware or data bottlenecks
Check the test range and its connection to real work
items.x: These checks target different failure modes. A precise arithmetic calculation does not resolve uncertainty about inputs, trend shape or what the measured quantity means.

items.p: ARC Prize reported GPT-6 Astra scores of 62.7% and 99.9% on the same ARC-AGI-3 evaluation set using two different harnesses. What comparison lesson follows?
o: The surrounding agent setup can materially change the measured result
The model's capability must have doubled between the two measurements
The higher result establishes competence at every real-world job
The lower result is invalid whenever a provider supplies another harness
ow: The reported comparison changes the harness, so it does not isolate a change in model capability.
A puzzle benchmark does not establish performance across all jobs.
Different harnesses can answer different evaluation questions; both need documentation.
keys: The surrounding agent setup can materially change the measured result
items.x: ARC Prize's September 2026 report describes a standard harness and a provider adapter preserving opaque reasoning state. Compare model, budget, setup and scoring together. A high result on this benchmark is not a general AGI certificate.

items.p: Epoch's April 2026 analysis found acceleration on three of four capability metrics, associated with reasoning models. What should a forecaster infer?
o: New methods can accelerate measured trends, with uncertain transfer
Each future benchmark must accelerate at the same rate
A past slowdown in one training method rules out the reported acceleration
A combined capability index directly measures economic automation
ow: Different tasks can respond differently to a new method.
Progress can use new methods as well as scaling an older one.
A capability index aggregates evaluation results, rather than measuring job automation.
keys: New methods can accelerate measured trends, with uncertain transfer
items.x: Epoch cautions that gains may be concentrated in tasks with checkable answers, such as math and code. An index can extend a ruler beyond individual benchmark saturation, while inheriting assumptions about which tests represent capability.

items.p: A task suite contains few well-measured long tasks, yet a model's estimated horizon lies far beyond them. How should that estimate be used?
o: As a fragile extrapolation that needs better long-task evidence
As a precise lower bound established by the longest fitted horizon
As proof the model can work independently for that many calendar hours
As grounds to discard all measurements from shorter tasks
ow: A point estimate beyond well-covered tasks need not establish a reliable lower bound.
Horizon uses human task time and a success threshold, rather than agent wall-clock duration.
Shorter-task evidence can remain informative even when long-horizon estimates are unstable.
keys: As a fragile extrapolation that needs better long-task evidence
items.x: METR's limitations note emphasizes wide uncertainty as its suite saturates. The relevant ceiling depends on the particular task suite and protocol; it is not a universal sixteen-hour limit on measuring AI. Report the tested range alongside the estimate.

items.p: Why does doubling an AI's 50% time horizon fail to establish that it doubles research productivity?
items.answer: Research productivity depends on supervision, checking, failure recovery and the mix of tasks. A horizon statistic alone does not measure those costs or overall output.
keys: horizons omit supervision and recovery costs
research output depends on more than task horizon

choice.p: Why does doubling an AI's 50% time horizon fail to establish that it doubles research productivity?
o: The statistic omits human oversight costs and the research workflow
A horizon is a direct measurement of overall research output
A 50% horizon guarantees success on all shorter research tasks
Models need no human checking once horizons exceed a workday
ow: A horizon measures performance on a task distribution at a success threshold.
Individual tasks vary; the aggregate statistic does not guarantee every shorter task.
A longer horizon does not establish reliability without checking.

items.x: Thomas Kwa's METR note says converting horizons to speedup needs richer workflow evidence, including prompting, checking and manual work. This connects the measurement problem back to the distinction between worker uplift and overall research acceleration.

items.p: Some developers decline a productivity trial because it requires working without AI. Among those who participate, measured gains are small. What is the best inference?
o: Selection may limit generalization, so the result needs other evidence
The small gain proves AI has little value for every developer
Refusal to participate proves the omitted developers have large measured gains
Random assignment eliminates the effect of who chose to enter the trial
ow: The participants may differ from developers who refused.
Their preferences suggest a possible selection mechanism without measuring its magnitude.
Randomization does not make the enrolled sample representative of nonparticipants.
keys: Selection may limit generalization, so the result needs other evidence
items.x: METR's February 2026 update describes this problem and treats its new productivity estimate as an unreliable signal of the current effect. A caveat can reduce confidence in a number without establishing a particular corrected value.

units.title: Why informed forecasters disagree
units.desc: Compare mechanisms behind longer and shorter timelines without turning a current failure into a permanent limit.

lessons.title: Find the crux, then seek discriminating evidence

items.p: Match each timeline crux to the question it raises.
pairs: How fast will organizations turn capabilities into routine productive use?
How much will better AI accelerate the development of better AI?
Will systems handle the long tail of errors in real work?
Can systems improve from experience and feedback on the job?
items.x: These are different questions. A forecaster can expect fast benchmark gains while expecting slower adoption, or strong research assistance without expecting self-sustaining acceleration. Name the mechanism before debating its arrival date.

items.p: In their November 2025 joint statement, what timing claim did AI 2027 and AI as Normal Technology authors agree on?
o: Strong AGI would probably not arrive before 2029
Strong AGI was more likely than not to arrive during 2027
Their disagreement prevented any shared near-term prediction
Strong AGI could be ruled out permanently on current evidence
ow: The statement distinguished a plausible fast scenario from their median expectations.
They endorsed a shared near-term view despite later disagreement.
The statement did not claim that strong AGI was impossible.
keys: the dated statement said strong AGI probably would not arrive before 2029
items.x: Their statement defined strong AGI in terms of robust human-level learning, adaptation and autonomy. Its shared expectation was dated November 2025, rather than a current consensus forecast. It illustrates why a scenario title can differ from its authors' probability distributions.

items.p: In his June 2025 argument for longer AGI timelines, why did Dwarkesh Patel emphasize continual learning?
items.answer: He argued that useful workers improve from experience and feedback, while the models he tested did not adapt comparably. Strong initial performance therefore did not establish that they could do whole jobs.
keys: learning from experience supports whole-job performance
Patel argued then-current models lacked comparable adaptation

choice.p: In his June 2025 argument for longer AGI timelines, why did Dwarkesh Patel emphasize continual learning?
o: Whole jobs require adaptation from experience beyond strong initial performance
Models must memorize every future task during their original pretraining
A larger context window mathematically guarantees learning like a human
A system must change its weights after every response to be economically useful
ow: Generalization can handle new tasks; memorizing all future work is not required.
More context can help without establishing the relevant learning ability.
This is stronger than Patel's argument and excludes other possible adaptation mechanisms.

items.x: Treat this as a dated, attributed bottleneck argument. Context, memory and additional training can all support forms of adaptation; the empirical question is whether a deployed system learns effectively enough for the jobs in question.

items.p: Narayanan and Kapoor distinguish fast method improvements from slow economic impact. Which evidence would most directly challenge their diffusion argument?
o: Broad, sustained adoption that reorganizes workflows and raises real output
A higher score on a short, automatically graded coding benchmark
A large increase in the amount of code generated before human review
A lab announcement redefining the word AGI around its newest model
ow: A capability score does not measure whether organizations have integrated the technology.
More generated code does not establish more useful work shipped.
A terminology change does not measure diffusion.
keys: Broad, sustained adoption that reorganizes workflows and raises real output
items.x: Their normal-technology argument emphasizes complementary institutions, workflows and organizational change. Broad adoption data are more directly relevant than another isolated capability demonstration, though measurement and causal attribution still matter.

items.p: Ege Erdil's April 2025 case for roughly twenty-year remote-work automation timelines emphasized experiment compute, data and economic trends. What would best test that case?
o: Evidence on research acceleration and reliable automation costs
A single model exceeding a benchmark that the forecast never used
An expert panel adopting a different verbal definition of AGI
A count of highly confident public predictions on either side
ow: An unrelated benchmark result may say little about the proposed bottlenecks.
A definition change affects comparisons without resolving the underlying mechanisms.
Confidence and popularity do not measure whether the bottlenecks bind.
keys: Evidence on research acceleration and reliable automation costs
items.x: Erdil argued that economic-growth trends would slow and that experimental compute and data constrain software-only acceleration. These were his views, rather than an institutional Epoch forecast. Revenue growth is relevant evidence, while differing milestones and bottlenecks still need separate checks.

units.title: Forecasting practice
units.desc: Score probabilities, assess the limits of track records, and read market prices without confusing them with facts.

items.p: Using the binary Brier loss (p minus outcome)^2, you forecast 80% and the event happens. A colleague forecasts 80% and it does not happen. What are the losses?
o: 0.04 for you and 0.64 for the colleague
0.20 for you and 0.80 for the colleague
0.04 for you and 0.36 for the colleague
0.80 for you and 0.20 for the colleague
ow: These are absolute gaps, rather than squared gaps.
The colleague's loss is 0.8 squared, which is 0.64.
These numbers do not apply the specified loss formula.
keys: 0.04 and 0.64 on the specified binary loss scale
items.x: The outcome is 1 for occurrence and 0 otherwise. Lower loss is better. Some implementations sum the squared errors across both outcomes and double this binary loss, so check the scoring convention before comparing published results.

items.p: You make twenty forecasts at 70%, and eighteen occur. What does this tell you about calibration?
o: Possible underconfidence, with limited evidence from twenty forecasts
It establishes precise calibration because a majority occurred
It establishes overconfidence because 70% exceeds an even chance
It proves your future 70% forecasts should all be changed to 90%
ow: Calibration compares observed frequency with the stated probability, rather than a simple majority.
The observed frequency exceeds the stated probability, which points in the opposite direction.
Sampling variation, question selection and correlation limit that extrapolation.
keys: outcomes more frequent than forecast, consistent with underconfidence
small or dependent sample limits certainty
items.x: At 70%, the expected count is fourteen; eighteen is 90% of this sample. Larger samples across comparable questions help distinguish miscalibration from chance. Correlated questions can provide less independent evidence than their count suggests.

items.p: Why use a proper probability scoring rule rather than count only whether a forecast was on the correct side of 50%?
items.answer: A proper rule rewards honest probabilities in expectation. Hit counting treats 51% and 99% alike when they predict the same outcome, so it cannot distinguish their confidence.
keys: honest probabilities optimize expected score or loss
hit counting ignores probability differences on the same side of 50%

choice.p: Why use a proper probability scoring rule rather than count only whether a forecast was on the correct side of 50%?
o: It evaluates confidence and makes honest probabilities optimal in expectation
It guarantees every low-probability event will eventually fail to happen
It gives all forecasters the same score whenever they predict the same side
It makes a single correct 99% forecast prove long-run calibration
ow: A 10% event can occur without the forecast being invalid.
Proper rules distinguish different probabilities even when they favor the same outcome.
Calibration concerns patterns across forecasts, rather than a single success.

items.x: For binary Brier loss, if your true probability is q, expected loss equals (p-q)^2 + q(1-q). It is minimized at p=q. Moving away from an honest probability raises expected loss, whether by hedging or exaggerating.

items.p: A planner predicts an AI tool rollout will succeed quickly because this team is unusually talented. What would a reference-class check add?
o: Outcomes and rollout times for comparable past projects
An assumption that the current team exactly matches every past project
A reason to discard all project-specific evidence after setting a base rate
A guarantee that historical adoption patterns will continue unchanged
ow: A reference class supplies a starting point, rather than identical cases.
Specific evidence can update a baseline.
Historical patterns inform uncertainty without guaranteeing continuity.
keys: Outcomes and rollout times for comparable past projects
items.x: The normal-technology view draws on previous technology diffusion; critics argue that unusually capable AI could change the reference class. A useful forecast makes that disagreement explicit and explains which features justify an update from the baseline.

items.p: A forecasting study associates accurate performance with frequent small updates. You then receive strong, decisive new evidence. What is the appropriate lesson?
o: Update in proportion to the evidence, even if the change is large
Keep each change small because small steps are always more accurate
Avoid updating because only the final forecast will be scored
Move toward the crowd regardless of what the evidence implies
ow: The observed association does not make a fixed small update correct for decisive evidence.
Keeping a forecast current matters even when it is scored later.
Crowd forecasts can inform judgment, but do not replace evaluation of the evidence.
keys: Update in proportion to the evidence, even if the change is large
items.x: Atanasov and colleagues found frequent, small revisions were associated with skill in a geopolitical tournament. That supports active updating and scrutiny of stubbornness; it does not establish a universal maximum update size.

items.p: A forecasting contest expected the best June 2022 MATH score to be 12.7%. Which result did its organizer report after resolution?
o: 50.3%, far above the forecast
12.9%, almost exactly the forecast
8%, below the forecast
95%, near saturation
ow: The reported result substantially exceeded the forecast.
The measured result was above, rather than below, the forecast.
The result was a substantial gain without nearing 95%.
keys: the reported MATH result was 50.3%
items.x: Jacob Steinhardt reported large misses on MATH and MMLU, while progress on an adversarial-robustness benchmark was slower than forecast. A resolved forecast can reveal errors without establishing that every future AI forecast should be shifted earlier.

items.p: FRI's 2026 review found repeated underestimation of benchmark progress, but noted that many reviewed questions resolved early. Why does that caveat matter?
o: Early successes are observed before later or unmet milestones can be scored
An early resolution makes a benchmark result automatically invalid
The review can establish economic impact from benchmark scores alone
Forecasts resolving after a deadline necessarily receive a better accuracy score
ow: A valid early resolution can still create selection effects in a partial track record.
The review explicitly separates benchmark progress from economic and societal impact.
Accuracy depends on the forecast and outcome, rather than late resolution automatically helping.
keys: Early successes are observed before later or unmet milestones can be scored
items.x: FRI reports benchmark underestimation, mixed adoption results and insufficient evidence on macro-scale impacts. Its near-term XPT analysis also found no statistically significant relationship between near-term accuracy and long-term risk forecasts. Transfer of forecasting skill is an empirical question.

items.p: Hypothetical: a Yes contract costs 9.5 cents and pays one dollar if a qualifying AI law is signed by December 31. What is the usual probability interpretation?
o: Roughly 9.5% for the event defined in the contract rules
Roughly 9.5% of traders believe some AI bill will pass
A 9.5-cent payout if any AI proposal reaches a committee
A guaranteed 9.5% chance that the event will occur
ow: A price is not a poll counting traders' views, and the event is a qualifying signed law.
The stipulated winning payout is one dollar; committee action is a different event.
Prices are estimates influenced by trading conditions, rather than guaranteed probabilities.
keys: Roughly 9.5% for the event defined in the contract rules
items.x: A price can summarize beliefs under suitable market conditions. Financing costs, fees, risk preferences and limited liquidity can affect that interpretation. The relevant event comes from the written resolution rules, rather than the headline alone.

items.p: Hypothetical: identical announcement criteria apply to two contracts. A displayed price is 41 cents for arrival by October and 38 cents for arrival by January after it. What should an analyst check?
o: Whether the prices are simultaneous executable quotes under comparable rules
Whether the later event can be less probable despite containing the earlier event
Whether the price gap establishes that traders expect an announcement retraction
Whether the display proves that thin trading caused inconsistent beliefs
ow: With identical criteria, the later deadline includes the earlier event.
A retraction matters only if the rules make it relevant; the stipulated events are nested.
Stale trades or bid-ask differences can create an apparent gap without proving that cause.
keys: Whether the prices are simultaneous executable quotes under comparable rules
items.x: For nested events, probability by the later deadline cannot be lower. Displayed last trades may be stale, and fees, spreads or contract details can prevent an apparent inconsistency from being an executable arbitrage. Verify those details before inferring a probability disagreement.

items.p: Why might a market on a company announcing AGI fail to answer when AI can reliably perform most jobs?
items.answer: An announcement and demonstrated job performance are different events. The contract also depends on its resolution rules and decision process.
keys: announcement differs from demonstrated capability
resolution rules define the contract event

choice.p: Why might a market on a company announcing AGI fail to answer when AI can reliably perform most jobs?
o: It resolves a specified announcement, which need not establish job capability
Every announcement contract requires a regulator to independently certify AGI
Market traders are prohibited from reading independent model evaluations
A company announcement automatically proves all candidate definitions of AGI
ow: Independent certification is required only if the rules specify it.
Forecasting platforms do not impose that blanket ban.
Different AGI definitions and claimed capabilities still require evaluation.

items.x: Polymarket's documentation distinguishes market titles from the rules and explains its resolution and dispute process. Apply the first unit's event-definition check before interpreting a market price as a timeline forecast.

units.title: What timelines imply for policy
units.desc: Compare attributed recommendations, distinguish forecasts from values, and design actions that can adapt to new evidence.

lessons.title: Act while preserving room to update

items.p: In his September 2026 testimony, Daniel Kokotajlo gave roughly even odds of automated AI research by the end of 2028. Which policy package did he recommend?
o: Transparency and less compute devoted to racing for research automation
Deferring oversight until an irreversible harm supplies conclusive evidence
Treating his forecast as a binding legal deadline for an industry-wide shutdown
Replacing model evaluations with market prices for announced AGI
ow: His recommendations sought earlier intervention and visibility.
He proposed policy changes, rather than that automatic legal rule.
He did not propose substituting announcement markets for evaluations.
keys: Transparency and less compute devoted to racing for research automation
items.x: This is his recommendation under his risk assessment and other assumptions. A short timeline can increase urgency without uniquely determining a policy: expected benefits, costs, risks and feasibility also matter.

items.p: Narayanan and Kapoor favor resilience as a response to AI risks. Which action best fits their stated logic?
o: Build technical and institutional capacity to reduce harm from shocks
Assume slow diffusion removes the need for any safety preparation
Make a single speculative arrival date the sole trigger for preparation
Treat every increase in benchmark performance as proof of societal harm
ow: Their argument supports preparation and harm reduction despite gradual-impact expectations.
Resilience can help across multiple timelines and kinds of shocks.
Benchmark gains do not establish particular harms.
keys: Build technical and institutional capacity to reduce harm from shocks
items.x: Their essay discusses democratic institutions, technical defenses, evidence gathering and government expertise. Resilience includes action before harm occurs to limit damage; it is broader than waiting to react after an incident.

items.p: Why do Narayanan and Kapoor question using precise AI existential-risk probabilities to justify public policy?
items.answer: They argue those estimates lack sufficiently validated methods, suitable reference classes and theory, so numerical precision can imply more evidential authority than is warranted.
keys: unvalidated methods and weak reference classes
numerical precision can overstate evidential support

choice.p: Why do Narayanan and Kapoor question using precise AI existential-risk probabilities to justify public policy?
o: They question the methods and justification behind those estimates
They think every numerical forecast is meaningless in principle
They think a probability below 50% establishes that a risk can be ignored
They argue benchmark progress cannot be forecast or scored
ow: Their essay explicitly distinguishes AI existential-risk estimates from forecasting in general.
A probability alone does not decide whether prevention is worthwhile.
They regard some capability forecasting as useful and participate in related efforts.

items.x: This is a contested methodological position, rather than a theorem that unprecedented events cannot be assigned probabilities. Their critique asks policymakers to inspect evidence and legitimacy of the inference. Near-term forecasting success alone does not validate a long-term catastrophe estimate.

items.p: Why does Karnofsky argue that capability-based if-then commitments can help people who disagree about AI timelines?
items.answer: People can agree that specified capabilities require mitigations without agreeing when those capabilities will arrive. The arrangement still needs timely detection and readiness to implement the mitigations.
keys: agree on capability-triggered protections without agreeing on dates
timely detection and implementation remain necessary

choice.p: Why does Karnofsky argue that capability-based if-then commitments can help people who disagree about AI timelines?
o: They tie safeguards to capabilities while leaving arrival dates uncertain
They guarantee evaluations will detect every dangerous capability before release
They require no preparation or expense until the exact trigger has been crossed
They remove disagreement about which risks and mitigations matter
ow: Detection is a challenge the framework must address.
Testing and developing mitigations can require advance resources and warning thresholds.
The framework still needs agreement on relevant capabilities and protections.

items.x: Karnofsky presents the approach as a potential bridge across timeline disagreements, with limits. Its usefulness depends on meaningful triggers, tests and credible implementation. Preparation may require lead time even if the capability arrives late.

items.p: Match each planning approach to its rationale in the cited arguments.
pairs: Toner: even a decade or two can leave little time to build capacity
Ord: broad uncertainty supports work that pays off at different times
Karnofsky: agree on conditional protections without fixing a date
Joint AI 2027 and normal-technology statement: improve evidence despite disagreement
items.x: These are planning approaches associated with their authors, rather than guarantees of policy effectiveness. The toolkit course covers particular instruments; the timeline question is how assumptions affect urgency, readiness and the value of new evidence.

units.title: Putting it together
units.desc: Use milestone definitions, causal measurement, market rules and uncertainty to assess realistic briefing requests.

items.p: Your member asks when AGI will arrive. A CEO says two years, a community forecast gives 2030, and an expert panel gives 2050. What should the briefing do first?
o: Align milestones and conditions before comparing their distributions
Average the dates and present the result as a consensus
Choose the CEO because internal access establishes the best forecast
Choose the latest date because cautious forecasts are more accurate
ow: Averages of different events and conditions need not describe a coherent forecast.
Internal access is relevant without automatically establishing accuracy.
Caution is not a substitute for comparing evidence and definitions.
keys: Align milestones and conditions before comparing their distributions
items.x: The LEAP timing statistic is conditional on panel agreement before 2100; other sources use different milestones and conditions. After aligning those, genuine disagreements about feedback, adoption and bottlenecks may remain. Do not attribute the entire spread to definitions.

items.p: Hypothetical: a lab says AI now leads 40% of its research tasks, up from 26%. Does that establish that a self-sustaining intelligence explosion has begun?
o: No: task share does not establish acceleration or feedback strength
Yes: crossing one-third of tasks is the theoretical tipping point
No: AI assistance cannot accelerate any part of AI research
Yes: the percentage directly states the speedup of the research frontier
ow: The feedback models do not supply that universal task-share threshold.
AI can contribute useful research without the evidence establishing an explosion.
The statistic classifies work; it does not measure the speed of overall progress.
keys: No: task share does not establish acceleration or feedback strength
items.x: Ask how the classification was made, how much supervision remains and whether AI caused sustained acceleration beyond other input changes. This combines the first unit's evidence check with the research-loop distinction between activity, worker uplift and progress.

items.p: Hypothetical: an AGI-announcement contract jumps from 38 to 55 cents on light trading. What should a briefing check before interpreting it as a capability update?
o: Resolution criteria, executable liquidity and relevant new evidence
Whether crossing 50 cents independently certifies that AGI exists
Whether the trading platform can replace direct model evaluation
Whether every trader changed their own probability by seventeen points
ow: A price crossing does not certify an outcome.
Markets summarize trading judgments without replacing the evidence they concern.
The same price move can arise from a few trades, and prices do not count traders' beliefs.
keys: Resolution criteria, executable liquidity and relevant new evidence
items.x: A contract may resolve on an announcement rather than demonstrated capability. Thin or stale quotes can also affect the displayed price. The relevant question is whether the movement conveys evidence about the milestone in your briefing.

items.p: A memo extrapolates a 16-hour horizon doubling every four months to a 2,000-work-hour project in about 2.5 years. What is the best assessment?
o: The arithmetic is close; measurement and project-level inference need support
The arithmetic fails because a 125-fold rise requires 125 doublings
The arithmetic establishes the model will reliably complete year-long projects
The arithmetic fails because the horizon only adds sixteen hours every four months
ow: A 125-fold rise needs about seven doublings.
The calculation assumes continued growth and says nothing by itself about job-level reliability.
The stated trend doubles, rather than adding a fixed increment.
keys: arithmetic is roughly correct
arithmetic does not establish measurement validity or reliable project completion
items.x: 16 times 2^7 is 2,048, reached after 28 months at the assumed rate. This is about a year of human work time, rather than an agent running for a calendar year. Long-task coverage, success rate, domain transfer and the future trend all need scrutiny.

items.p: Your boss wants one transformative-AI date to anchor a ten-year strategy. What should a useful alternative briefing provide?
items.answer: A defined milestone with an attributed probability range, the assumptions driving it and a plan tested across earlier and later arrival, including evidence that would trigger revision.
keys: defined milestone and attributed uncertainty range
plan across earlier and later arrival with update triggers

choice.p: Your boss wants one transformative-AI date to anchor a ten-year strategy. What should a useful alternative briefing provide?
o: A named milestone, a probability range and plans that adapt to specified evidence
The mean of every published date, without adjusting for different event definitions
The most vivid published scenario, treated as the central forecast
A promise to delay planning until the timing uncertainty has disappeared
ow: Combining incompatible dates can obscure the actual forecast target.
Vividness does not establish a scenario's probability or representativeness.
Uncertainty can persist while preparation takes time.

items.x: Ord argues for broad timeline distributions and a portfolio of work; Toner emphasizes preparation lead times. Use those planning ideas while keeping judgments about benefits, costs and acceptable risks explicit. A forecast informs a decision without choosing the values behind it.

timelines.description: Define forecast events, compare evidence about AI progress, and evaluate predictions with uncertainty and scoring rules.
caveat: Source-checked October 23, 2026 by AI reviewers; no human has reviewed this draft. Forecasts are attributed, conditional and uncertain. Historical measurements do not establish future growth. Market-price examples are hypothetical. Research findings are specific to their tested settings.
Drafted and independently reviewed by AI. No person has reviewed it.
timelines.meta: 8 units | AI reviewed; no human review

uschina.name: US-China AI Relations and Verification

units.title: The map: capability, rules and diplomacy
units.desc: Separate what models can do, what domestic rules require, and what the governments have announced. Then ask what evidence would verify a commitment.

lessons.title: The map and China's public-service rules

items.p: Match each question in US-China AI relations to the kind of evidence needed.
pairs: Model evaluations and information about developers
Domestic laws and their stated scope
Is an agreed limit being followed?
Evidence of compliance and checks for hidden activity
items.x: Keep capability, domestic regulation, diplomacy and verification separate. A benchmark result does not establish treaty compliance; a diplomatic announcement does not establish an operational inspection system.

items.p: Match each Chinese developer to its model family, without assuming a fixed capability ranking.
items.x: Alibaba, Moonshot and Z.ai are three developers to recognize alongside DeepSeek. Release versions and rankings change quickly. Nationality, release strategy and benchmark results answer different questions.

items.p: China's 2023 rules for generative AI (the Interim Measures) are binding. What activity do they cover?
o: Generative AI services offered to the public in China
Any training run above a fixed amount of computing power
Military and government use of AI, leaving commercial services alone
Models sold abroad, which need an export license first
ow: The Interim Measures apply based on offering generative AI services to the domestic public, rather than a training-compute cutoff.
They cover services to the public. Groups that develop AI without offering it to the public are exempt.
The Measures regulate services inside China and set no export licensing for models.
keys: generative AI services offered to the domestic public in China
items.x: Article 2 excludes development and use that do not provide generative AI services to the domestic public. Article 17 requires security assessments and algorithm filing for services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilization capacity. That scope differs from a universal licensing rule for training models.

items.p: A Chinese chatbot provider cites a voluntary safety framework as proof it has met all legal duties. What should a reviewer check next?
keys: distinguish voluntary guidance from applicable binding obligations
items.x: China's binding generative AI measures, content-labeling rules and non-binding safety guidance serve different functions. A risk framework can inform practice without replacing legal compliance.
items.answer: Check the binding rules that apply to the service and whether the provider meets them. Citing a voluntary safety framework alone does not establish legal compliance.

o: Applicable binding rules and the service's compliance with them
Whether the framework discusses enough separate categories of AI risk
Whether a foreign evaluator has ranked the model above US competitors
Whether the developer has published weights for external researchers
ow: A broad risk taxonomy does not establish compliance with binding obligations.
A foreign capability ranking does not decide whether domestic service obligations are met.
Publishing weights does not establish that a public service meets legal duties.

items.p: China's AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 discusses loss of control and weapons misuse. What can a staffer infer from that document?
o: These risks appear in guidance; enforceable duties need a separate legal basis
It sets a binding compute line above which labs need a state license to train
It treats catastrophic risk as a Western worry that Chinese regulators won't address
It covers only content risks such as rumors, leaving weapons risks to the army
ow: The framework is technical guidance; it does not create the licensing rule in this option.
The framework explicitly discusses loss of control.
The framework includes weapons-related risks alongside content and other risks.
keys: recognition of frontier risks in non-binding guidance
separate binding duties require a legal basis
items.x: Framework 2.0, released in September 2025, includes loss-of-control and weapons-related risks. Its status as a technical governance framework differs from the binding Interim Measures. Recognizing a risk in guidance does not establish a training-license system or prove enforcement.

items.p: Why might an AI company release downloadable weights while still charging for hosted access?
o: Wider adoption can build demand for hosting and related services
Chinese law requires frontier developers to publish weights so regulators can inspect them
Open release exempts a model from China's filing and content rules for public chatbots
Published weights can't be copied or altered, so release protects a lab's methods
ow: The Interim Measures regulate public-facing services; they do not require developers to publish weights.
China's 2023 rules turn on offering a service to the public in China, however the model is released.
The reverse: anyone with the weights can copy and fine-tune them, which is why release can't be undone.
keys: wider adoption can support hosted access or complementary services
items.x: Epoch AI describes model diffusion and revenue as competing goals for Chinese labs. It also notes that Alibaba and ByteDance can earn through complementary businesses such as cloud services and advertising. This is a business-strategy interpretation, not a legal requirement or a guarantee of profit.

items.p: In the US readout of the May 2024 Geneva AI talks, officials exchanged views and raised concerns. What did that establish?
o: Government contact on AI risk, without demonstrating an enforceable safety regime
A jointly enforceable set of model-testing duties for both countries' frontier labs
Reciprocal access for government evaluators to inspect each country's AI systems
A verified limit on training compute, implemented through agreed on-site checks
ow: An exchange of views does not establish binding model-testing duties.
The US readout describes discussion, not an inspection arrangement.
The readout does not announce a verified compute limit.
keys: exchange of views on AI risk
contact does not establish enforceable or verified limits
items.x: The US readout records discussion of AI safety, risk management and US concerns about misuse, including by China. Treat official descriptions of discussion as evidence of contact; stronger claims require agreement text and implementation evidence.

items.p: At their November 2024 meeting in Lima, what did Biden and Xi affirm about AI and nuclear weapons?
o: Keeping human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons
A ban on any AI use in nuclear early-warning and command systems
A treaty, with inspections, barring AI from nuclear launch decisions
A plan for joint exercises on AI failures in nuclear command
ow: They spoke to the decision to use nuclear weapons; other AI uses in nuclear systems weren't addressed.
It was a political statement in a leaders' readout, with no treaty text or verification.
No exercises were agreed; the leaders also called for developing military AI 'in a prudent and responsible manner.'
keys: human control over decisions to use nuclear weapons
items.x: The November 2024 Lima readout affirms human control over nuclear-use decisions. It does not specify a verification procedure or ban every use of AI in nuclear systems. The distinction between a stated norm and a checked commitment recurs in the verification units.

items.p: As of October 23, 2026, what two AI mechanisms did the September US-China summit readouts announce?
items.answer: A bilateral dialogue on AI risks and benefits, and an agreement to establish a communication channel for AI incidents.
keys: dialogue on AI risks and benefits
agreement to establish a bilateral AI incident channel
items.x: The White House calls it the Super Intelligence Dialogue and says the next exchange will occur by November 2026; China's readout calls it an AI dialogue and says November. Both announce an incident channel without detailed operating procedures. The announcement alone does not show an operational channel.

choice.p: Which two AI mechanisms did the September 2026 summit readouts announce?
o: An AI risk-and-benefit dialogue and an agreement to establish an incident channel
A joint cap on frontier training compute, to be checked by short-notice inspections
Mutual pre-release testing of each other's frontier models by government labs
An end to US chip export controls in exchange for more Chinese rare earth exports
ow: These readouts do not announce a compute cap or inspection regime.
These readouts do not announce reciprocal pre-release model testing.
The announced AI mechanisms are dialogue and incident communication; no such exchange is stated.

items.p: A briefing cites a CCTV-linked commentator's AI proposals as obligations China accepted in the September 2026 summit. What is the key correction?
o: Separate commentary proposals from commitments in the official readouts
Treat state-linked commentary as more binding than a government readout
Assume proposals mentioned after a summit were part of a confidential treaty
Infer that an incident channel authorizes inspections of Chinese data centers
ow: State linkage does not turn commentary into an accepted obligation.
Timing does not establish the existence or content of a treaty.
A communication channel does not by itself confer inspection rights.
keys: distinguish commentary from official commitments
items.x: Yuyuantantian commentary, translated by Pekingnology, proposes risk definitions and incident-reporting procedures. The official readouts announce dialogue and a channel. Commentary can signal priorities, while the scope of a commitment needs stronger evidence.

items.p: In September 2026, US government testers assessed Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.3. Which conclusion matches their cyber benchmarks?
o: Leading among open weights, behind the current US frontier on these tests
Far behind: about two years behind top US models on every cyber test it was given
Ahead of every US model it tested, the first Chinese model to lead on cyber
Unscored, because Z.ai refused to give the testers access to the model
ow: CAISI estimated a gap of about four months on its aggregate cyber measure.
It still trailed current US frontier models; it led only among open-weight models.
Z.ai released the weights publicly; CAISI reported benchmark results.
keys: led released open-weight models on CAISI cyber benchmarks
trailed current US frontier models on those tests
items.x: CAISI reported that GLM-5.3 led released open-weight models on its cyber tests and lagged the US frontier by about four months on its aggregate measure. This is a dated, task-specific estimate, not a general measure of China's AI capabilities.

units.title: Lessons from arms control
units.desc: How the hotline, New START and the chemical weapons treaty worked in practice, and why AI is harder to check than missiles or chemical plants.

items.p: New START inspections were paused in 2020, and Russia later refused to facilitate their resumption. What lesson does this offer AI negotiators?
o: Inspection rights need sustained access and cooperation to produce evidence
Treaty inspection rights ensure access even when either government objects
Satellite observations can replace every kind of information lost from visits
Once inspections stop, the treaty's original declaration remains sufficient
ow: A legal obligation can be breached; it does not physically guarantee access.
Remote observations and visits reveal different kinds of information.
Old declarations lose value as forces or facilities change.
keys: legal inspection rights need practical access and cooperation
items.x: New START permitted on-site inspections. Russia's refusal to facilitate them impaired verification before the treaty expired in February 2026. The AI analogy is limited: legal access rights and the practical ability to exercise them are separate design problems.

items.p: By July 2025, the OPCW reported no requested CWC challenge inspections, despite conducting other special missions. What should AI negotiators learn from this?
o: A treaty mechanism can exist without states choosing to invoke it
An unused mechanism proves that treaty members committed no violations
Ad hoc missions establish that standing challenge rights are legally void
Formal challenge inspections are the same process as routine plant visits
ow: Non-use does not establish the absence of violations.
Alternative missions do not erase treaty rights.
Routine visits and challenge inspections have different mandates and procedures.
keys: formal availability differs from actual use
items.x: The OPCW's July 2025 readiness note distinguishes never-requested challenge inspections from ad hoc operations in several countries. An AI regime would need procedures, capacity and political willingness to use its rights.

items.p: The 1963 Washington-Moscow 'hotline,' set up after the Cuban missile crisis, was a teletype link. Why did officials choose written messages over a phone line?
items.answer: Written messages avoided misunderstandings from hurried spoken translation and gave leaders time to think before replying, which mattered for a link meant to keep a crisis or accident from escalating to war.
keys: avoid misunderstanding from rapid spoken translation
time to reflect before responding
items.x: The 1963 hotline used written communication. Its purpose was to reduce the risk of escalation through misunderstanding. For an AI channel, speed, translation and clear written incident records are practical design choices.

choice.p: Why was the 1963 Washington-Moscow hotline a teletype link instead of a telephone?
o: Written messages cut misreadings from hurried translation and gave leaders time to think
Calls across the Atlantic were too unreliable in 1963, so text was the only workable option
Teletype could be encrypted, while a phone call could be tapped by third countries
A written record let each side publish the exchanges to show it had acted in good faith
ow: Officials chose text on purpose, to avoid misunderstanding between leaders; the reason given wasn't technical.
Security wasn't the stated reason; the concern was leaders misreading each other.
The hotline was designed for direct crisis communication rather than public exchanges.

items.p: Match each historical mechanism to the AI governance function it could help negotiators think about.
pairs: Counting declared AI chips against an agreed inventory
Short-notice access to a site suspected of hiding a data center
Checking that a country's list of declared facilities is complete
A direct line so an AI accident isn't mistaken for an attack
items.x: These are analogies, not existing AI treaty powers. Inspections check declarations, additional access helps investigate undeclared activity, and crisis communication serves a different task from compliance checking.

lessons.title: Why AI is harder to check

items.p: Why is counting a data center's chips insufficient to establish that it obeyed a limit on training-run compute?
items.answer: The same chips can perform permitted or prohibited workloads. Inspectors also need evidence of how much computation each relevant run used, rather than just the installed hardware count.
keys: same chips support permitted and prohibited workloads
need run-level compute-use evidence
items.x: Hardware inventories bound available capacity, while records or monitoring address how that capacity was used. Compute-monitoring proposals combine both. A cap defined by compute differs from a rule about harmful model behavior.

choice.p: Why is counting a data center's chips insufficient to establish that it obeyed a limit on training-run compute?
o: The same chips support different runs, so workload evidence is also needed
International law forbids inspecting data centers, unlike missile bases
AI chips can't be counted, because they carry no serial numbers
Training runs finish in hours, too fast for inspectors to catch
ow: Data center inspections are a standard proposal, modeled on New START and IAEA visits.
Chips can be counted and could carry unique identifiers; the problem is seeing what they compute.
Frontier training uses thousands of chips for months; verification proposals target exactly that scale.

items.p: Iraq once ran a secret nuclear weapons program while IAEA inspections covered only the facilities Iraq had declared. What's the equivalent weak spot in an AI agreement?
o: Declared-site checks alone can miss clusters the state never reported
Inspectors could check a site's chips but not how much electricity it draws
A state could stop its own AI labs from publishing their safety research
Declared data centers would be open to inspection only once a year
ow: Power use can be metered and is a proposed check; the deeper gap is compute that was never reported.
Publication isn't what verification checks; the gap is undeclared compute.
Some proposals add continuous monitoring at declared sites; the harder problem is sites never declared.
keys: check declarations for completeness as well as correctness
items.x: The IAEA's experience in Iraq and North Korea exposed the limits of concentrating on declared material and facilities. The Additional Protocol expanded information and access for detecting undeclared activity. AI proposals face a similar completeness problem.

items.p: Some verification researchers argue a regime should track AI chips from the factory onward, instead of relying mainly on hunting for hidden data centers. What's their main reason?
o: It targets a concentrated supply chain before chips disperse among sites
Hidden data centers can't be found with satellites, heat imaging or power data
Chips already report their own workloads, so tracking them reveals every training run
Data centers are private property, which international treaties can't cover
ow: Remote sensing can spot large sites; the worry is concealment and dispersal across small sites.
Reliable workload reporting requires additional verification mechanisms; location information alone cannot establish use.
Treaties can cover private sites, as chemical weapons inspections of commercial plants show.
keys: a concentrated supply chain can be monitored before chips disperse among sites
items.x: Scher and Thiergart propose tracking chips as well as monitoring their use. Their concern is that multiple smaller sites can contribute to one workload. Supply-chain monitoring would still need broad participation, safeguards and checks on undeclared hardware.

items.p: The Chemical Weapons Convention makes a challenged state give inspectors access to a site, while letting it protect sensitive installations. Why would an AI inspection regime need a similar balance?
items.answer: Data centers and labs hold a country's most sensitive AI assets, such as model weights, code and training data, which a rival could steal or learn from. Inspectors need enough access to confirm facts, like chip counts or that no banned run is under way, without seeing those secrets.
keys: sites hold weights, code and data a rival would want
access limited to what proves compliance, protecting secrets
items.x: Article IX of the CWC pairs relevant access with protection for unrelated confidential information. AI proposals similarly need enough evidence to check compliance while protecting model weights, code and data. This balance can constrain which checks are feasible.

choice.p: Why would an AI inspection regime need to limit what inspectors can see?
o: Sites hold secrets like model weights, so access should stop at what proves compliance
Inspectors lack AI expertise, so detailed access would only confuse their reports
Running AI chips make data centers too hazardous for outsiders to walk through
Limiting access lets the host state rule on its own compliance without outside review
ow: Expertise is a real need, but the reason for limits is protecting secrets.
Hazard isn't the issue; arms inspectors routinely visit far more dangerous sites.
Limits narrow what inspectors see; they don't hand the host the final judgment.

units.title: The verification toolkit
units.desc: What each way of checking an AI agreement can and can't catch, from satellites and whistleblowers to inspections and on-chip mechanisms, and how they cover each other's gaps.

items.p: What can satellite imagery, power-use evidence and customs records most directly help investigate in an AI agreement?
o: Possible large computing sites and hardware flows
Which model a known data center is training this month
Whether a Chinese model has dangerous bioweapons skills
Whether a detected training run complied with the treaty's compute cap
ow: Remote methods see buildings, heat and power; seeing workloads needs access or on-chip mechanisms.
Capabilities need model evaluations, which require access to the model itself.
Hardware and power clues alone do not establish run-level compute accounting.
keys: possible computing sites and hardware flows
items.x: These are proposed clues to undeclared computing capacity. They generally cannot establish the workload inside a site, and visibility varies with data access and concealment. Use this layer to guide further investigation rather than certify compliance.

items.p: Proposals for verifying an AI agreement often include whistleblower programs, modeled on the SEC's cash awards. Name two reasons such a program could fail against a state determined to cheat.
items.answer: Examples: the state can physically or digitally block staff from contacting verifiers; staff fear retaliation; a small, loyal team can run the violation, leaving few people who could leak; reports can be incomplete or false and hard to check.
keys: the state can block contact with verifiers
fear of retaliation
small, loyal teams leave few potential leakers
reports may be unreliable
items.x: Personnel-based verification proposals include protected reporting and regular private contact with verifiers. Rewards alone cannot remove retaliation risk or guarantee reliable reports. These problems can arise in either country.

choice.p: Which is a reason a whistleblower program could fail against a state determined to cheat on an AI agreement?
o: The state can block staff from reaching verifiers and punish those who try
Whistleblowers can report on chips, but not on models or training runs
Paying informants is barred by treaty, so no rewards can be offered
Small projects necessarily disclose violations through their staffing records
ow: Insiders can report anything they know about, including models, code and how data centers are used.
Award programs like the SEC's are the model proposals build on; the real obstacle is suppression.
Staffing records do not establish whether a violation occurred; a small loyal team may reduce the chance of disclosure.

items.p: A proposed agreement relies on new chip-based workload certificates. What rollout problem must negotiators address?
o: Legacy hardware and resistance to tampering by well-resourced adversaries
The logs would expose each company's full code and data to the other side's inspectors
The features would work only on US-made chips, since China designs no AI chips of its own
Chipmakers have declined to add security features to the AI chips they've sold since 2024
ow: Confidentiality is a design goal, though it must be demonstrated for the chosen protocol.
China has its own AI chips, such as Huawei's Ascend line, so its chipmakers would need to take part too.
Some security primitives already exist; their existence does not establish a complete verification system.
keys: legacy hardware coverage
tamper resistance requires development and testing
items.x: Hardware-backed verification is a research proposal with implementation and security gaps. Existing security features do not automatically provide treaty-grade workload verification. Coverage of previously deployed chips must be addressed separately.

items.p: In a proposed deal, mutually accepted hardware attests execution of agreed safety tests on a declared model and shares results while hiding its weights. What remains unproven?
o: That the tested model is the one actually deployed, or that no undeclared model exists
Whether the model scores above an agreed danger threshold on the tests that were run
That the agreed test code ran inside the attested environment
Its results, which the secure hardware keeps hidden from both sides
ow: That is exactly what the tests measure, provided the right model was tested and the tests are good.
Under the stipulated security assumptions, attestation establishes execution of the agreed code, while model identity across deployment remains a separate question.
Confidential computing hides the weights; the agreed test results can still be shared.
keys: tested model may differ from the deployed model
undeclared models are outside the test
items.x: A secure evaluation protocol must establish model identity as well as protect the test and the model. Agreed tests also have limits. Passing a test on a declared model cannot rule out separate undeclared development.

items.p: Put this simplified compute-accounting argument in logical order, after the agreement defines prohibited runs.
items: Identify relevant computing capacity, including linked sites
Verify which chip-hours were used for permitted workloads
Bound remaining unverified computation
Compare that bound with the compute needed for a prohibited run
items.x: This is a logical argument, not a universal inspection timetable. Scher and Thiergart describe bounding unverified chip-hours; distributed workloads and hardware or algorithm changes complicate that bound.

items.p: Match each verification method to a way a determined cheater could get around it.
pairs: Capacity may be concealed or difficult to classify
Domestic production may not appear in import records
The host may alter evidence before access
Legacy chips can remain outside the system
Retaliation or blocked contact may deter disclosure
items.x: Different layers may help address one another's gaps, but coverage is incomplete and failures can be correlated. A host denying access could impair several checks together. Layering requires checking what each source adds.

units.title: Putting it to work
units.desc: Mixed cases that draw on the whole course: an attack traced to a Chinese model, what the new incident channel should carry, and judging draft verification clauses.

items.p: An AI agent breaks into a US hospital network, and forensics show it ran on a Chinese open-weight model. A senator says this proves Beijing ordered the attack. What's the key caution?
items.answer: Model origin alone does not identify the attacker. Anyone with access to downloadable weights may run a copy. Attribution needs separate evidence linking the operation to an actor.
keys: model origin alone does not establish the attacker
downloadable weights can be used by third parties
attribution needs separate evidence
items.x: Open weights allow third parties to run copies outside the developer's service. This scenario separates a capability fact from an attribution claim. Crisis communication may help exchange evidence, while responsibility still needs investigation.

choice.p: An AI agent attack on a US hospital ran on a Chinese open-weight model. What's the key caution before blaming Beijing?
o: Anyone can download and run open weights, so the model's origin doesn't identify the attacker
China's AI rules bar Chinese models from use abroad, so the forensic evidence must be faked
Open-weight models report their use to the developer, so Beijing would already know the attacker
Only a state agency could run a model this large, so a government must be behind it
ow: China's rules govern services offered in China; they can't stop downloaded weights being used abroad.
Running downloaded weights does not inherently report activity to the original developer.
Model access alone does not establish state sponsorship.

items.p: A bilateral AI channel exists, but each side must seek senior approval before sending even an urgent notice. Which design change most directly addresses delay?
o: Agree in advance who can send notices and what triggers them
Add an annual joint report summarizing completed diplomatic meetings
Publish the model weights involved before either side sends a notice
Replace notification procedures with broad statements supporting safety
ow: An annual summary does not resolve authorization for urgent notices.
Weight release adds security risks and does not resolve notice authority.
General principles leave the authorization problem unresolved.
keys: pre-agreed authority and incident triggers reduce avoidable delay
items.x: A channel needs usable operating procedures as well as an announcement. This hypothetical applies the earlier distinction between formal commitments and implementation. CNAS recommends defining serious incidents that warrant prompt notification.

items.p: CNAS analysts recommend incident communication without sharing capability-enhancing details. Which proposed message best fits that goal?
o: Prompt notice of serious incidents at agreed severity levels, minus capability details
Swapping frontier model weights so each side can run its own tests on the other's systems
A joint cap on training compute, with the channel used for each side's compliance reports
Notice of any AI malfunction either side detects, however minor, within 24 hours
ow: Sharing weights could expose capability-relevant information, contrary to the stated goal.
A compute cap is a different commitment from incident communication.
Prompt reporting needs an agreed seriousness threshold; reporting every malfunction would create noise.
keys: serious incident notice with agreed severity and timing
protect capability-enhancing details
items.x: This is a policy recommendation, not an agreed bilateral reporting standard. CNAS proposes shared terminology and prompt notice of serious incidents while protecting capability-relevant information. Both governments would still need to agree on scope and procedures.

items.p: A hypothetical treaty caps training runs at 10^27 operations and requires annual reports of each side's largest run. It adds no audit or completeness checks. What is the central verification gap?
o: It relies on unchecked self-reports and can't detect undeclared compute
A compute limit can't be defined precisely enough to write into a treaty
Yearly reports would reveal too much about each side's secret methods
It caps training runs when it should cap how many AI chips each side owns
ow: A threshold can be defined, though accounting conventions must be specified; this clause's gap is unchecked reporting.
A single yearly number reveals little; the problem is that nothing checks it.
A chip cap would face the same problem: without verification, it rests on trust.
keys: unchecked accuracy of declarations
no completeness check for undeclared activity
items.x: The clause supplies claims without a way to check their accuracy or completeness. Earlier units separated declared-site checks from searches for undeclared capacity. An improved clause would need evidence for both, with appropriate confidentiality protections.

items.p: A draft AI agreement lets each side inspect any suspected data center within 30 days of a request. Why might negotiators push for much shorter notice?
items.answer: Thirty days gives the host time to move chips, change workloads or alter evidence before inspectors arrive. Shorter notice reduces that opportunity, though it does not guarantee detection.
keys: long notice creates opportunities to conceal or alter evidence
shorter notice reduces that opportunity
items.x: Short notice reduces opportunities to change evidence, while preserving relevant records and combining checks remain necessary. CWC Article IX provides an inspection precedent; it does not determine the notice period of a future AI agreement.

choice.p: Why might negotiators push for much shorter notice than 30 days to inspect a suspected AI data center?
o: A month lets the host move chips, change workloads and alter logs before a visit
Data center leases run month to month, so a site may change owners within 30 days
AI chips wear out within weeks under heavy use, destroying the physical evidence
International law caps treaty notice periods at two weeks for any type of inspection
ow: Ownership isn't the issue; the risk is the host hiding evidence of a banned run.
AI chips last years; the evidence at risk is logs and where the chips are, which a host can change.
Notice periods are negotiated treaty by treaty; New START and the chemical weapons treaty set their own.

uschina.description: From incentives and diplomacy to agreements, verification and the limits of evidence about compliance.
caveat: Revised and source-checked October 23, 2026 by AI reviewers; no person has reviewed it. Historical treaty examples are analogies. AI verification mechanisms are proposals with important technical and political limits. Hypothetical clauses are labeled.
uschina.meta: 4 units | AI reviewed; no human review

alignment.name: Alignment (sample)

units.title: Training signals and generalization
units.desc: Build a map, study a concrete case, then apply the distinction.

items.p: Technical alignment research splits into a few big problems. Match each problem to the question it asks.
pairs: Does the feedback reward the behavior people actually want?
Will behavior still pursue the intended goal in new situations?
How can people supervise work they cannot check unaided?
Could apparently good behavior conceal an unwanted objective?
items.x: These are four useful questions for organizing alignment research. They overlap: stronger oversight can improve feedback, while tests in new situations can expose goals that training did not distinguish. The technical term inner alignment is narrower in its original formulation: it concerns objectives of learned optimizers.

items.p: Researchers trained a game-playing AI to collect a coin that always sat at the right end of each level. Then they moved the coin to random spots. What did the agent do?
o: Ran skillfully to the right end of each level, usually ignoring the coin
Searched each level until it found the coin, wherever it had been placed
Stopped moving, since nothing it saw matched the levels it had trained on
Wandered at random, having lost the skills it had learned in training
ow: It had learned 'go right', which matched 'get the coin' in every training level.
It kept playing competently; its skills carried over and only its goal was off.
Its skills survived, which is what makes this failure worrying: a capable agent pursuing the wrong goal.
